definition_zh: 失败；失败的人或事；故障；未做到
definition_en: a lack of success; a person or thing that is unsuccessful; a breakdown in a machine or system; the fact of not doing something required
core_image: 一场努力最终没有抵达终点
scene: 停电使机器全部停止运转。 The power failure stopped all the machines.
sceneCN: 这里 failure 是「故障」（第 3 个义项）；句意：停电使机器全部停止运转。

senses.title: A lack of success
senses.definition: a lack of success in achieving something
senses.definitionCN: 在达成某事上缺乏成功
senses.example: The project ended in failure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目以失败告终。
senses.why: The base sense is the general state of not succeeding.
senses.whyCN: 基础义是未能成功的总体状态。

senses.title: An unsuccessful person or thing
senses.definition: a person or thing that is unsuccessful
senses.definitionCN: 不成功的人或事物
senses.example: The film was a complete failure.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影彻底失败了。
senses.why: The abstract state becomes a countable instance.
senses.whyCN: 抽象状态变成可数的具体例子。

senses.title: A breakdown
senses.definition: a breakdown in a machine, system, or organ
senses.definitionCN: 机器、系统或器官的故障
senses.example: A power failure closed the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 一次停电让机场关闭。
senses.why: A thing that cannot work has failed its purpose.
senses.whyCN: 无法工作的东西就是未能履行职责。

senses.title: An omission
senses.definition: the fact of not doing something that is required
senses.definitionCN: 没有做被要求做的事情
senses.example: His failure to reply annoyed them.
senses.exampleCN: 他未回复让他们很恼火。
senses.why: Not doing a duty is a failure to meet it.
senses.whyCN: 未履行义务就是未能达到要求。

intro.en: Failure comes from Anglo-French failer plus the noun ending -ure.
intro.cn: failure 由盎格鲁-法语 failer 加名词后缀 -ure 构成。

items.en: Fallere means to deceive or disappoint.
items.cn: fallere 意为欺骗或使人失望。

items.en: Faillir means to miss or lack.
items.cn: faillir 意为错过或欠缺。

items.en: Failer becomes the legal verb form.
items.cn: failer 成为法律语境中的动词形式。

items.en: Failure names the state of falling short.
items.cn: 十七世纪 failure 指未达标的状况。

items.en: Failure also names machine breakdowns.
items.cn: 现代英语中 failure 也指机器故障。

note.en: Failure is the result; fail is the action.
note.cn: failure 是结果，fail 则是动作。

entries.definition: to not succeed
an important part or quality
a fixed piece of equipment
the state of losing a contest
a failure of a machine or system
a complete failure

normalIntro.en: Failure is the noun for every kind of fail.
normalIntro.cn: failure 是各种 fail 的名词形式。

normal.en: Failure is often the first step to success.
normal.cn: 失败常常是成功的第一步。

normal.en: The experiment was a failure.
normal.cn: 这次实验失败了。

normal.en: A power failure darkened the city.
normal.cn: 一次停电让城市陷入黑暗。

normal.en: His failure to appear worried us.
normal.cn: 他没有出现让我们担心。

normal.en: The failure rate of the device is low.
normal.cn: 这个设备的故障率很低。

abstract.en: Picture a rocket falling back to the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象火箭落回地面。

abstract.en: Imagine a bridge that never reaches the far bank.
abstract.cn: 想象一座始终到不了对岸的桥。

abstract.en: Think of a lamp suddenly going dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯突然熄灭。

examples.en: He learned more from failure than from success.
examples.cn: 他从失败中学到的比从成功中学到的更多。

examples.en: The engine failure forced an emergency landing.
examples.cn: 引擎故障迫使飞机紧急降落。

examples.en: Her failure to sign the form caused a delay.
examples.cn: 她未在表格上签字造成了延误。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 动词变名词
dict_mnemonic.text: fail（失败）+ -ure（名词后缀）= failure（失败），与 nature、pressure 的构词方式相同。

root: failure 由 fail（失败）加名词后缀 -ure 构成，最终源自拉丁语 fallere（使人失望）。

sensesIntro.en: Failure is lack of success, an unsuccessful thing, a breakdown, or an omission.
sensesIntro.cn: failure 指不成功、失败的人或事、故障，或未做到某事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an effort that never reaches its goal.
core.cn: 核心意象：始终没有抵达目标的努力。

branches.en: The base sense is lack of success.
branches.cn: 基础义是缺乏成功。

branches.en: The state becomes a countable failure.
branches.cn: 状态变成可数的失败实例。

branches.en: A machine failure is a breakdown.
branches.cn: 机器 failure 就是故障。

branches.en: Failure to act is an omission.
branches.cn: 未行动就是一种疏忽。

branches.en: Broken systems and broken plans share the word.
branches.cn: 坏掉的系统与落空的计划共用一词。

intro.en: The suffix -ure turns the verb fail into a noun of result.
intro.cn: 后缀 -ure 把动词 fail 变成表示结果的名词。

latinIntro.en: Failure traces through French to Latin fallere, to deceive.
latinIntro.cn: failure 经由法语追溯到拉丁语 fallere（欺骗）。

items.meaning: lack of success or a breakdown

items.exampleCN: 她始终如一的善意帮助了我们。

items.meaning: safe even if a part fails
items.example: The reactor has a fail-safe design.
items.exampleCN: 反应堆采用故障安全设计。

items.meaning: the heart's inability to pump properly
items.exampleCN: 心力衰竭需要谨慎治疗。

items.example: The power failure lasted an hour.
The failure rate fell after the fix.

latinEntries.example: Fallere is the source of fail and false.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fallere 是 fail 与 false 的源头。

definition_zh: 系上；附上；认为有（重要性）
definition_en: to fasten one thing to another, or to connect value or feeling to it
core_image: 用别针把两张纸别在一起
scene: 填表时她随手把照片别在右上角。 She attached a photo to the form.
sceneCN: 这里 attach 是「附上」（第 1 个义项：把东西固定到另一件东西上）；句意是她把照片附在表格上。

senses.title: Fasten one thing to another
senses.definition: to fasten or join one thing to another
senses.definitionCN: 把一件东西固定或连接到另一件上
senses.example: She attached a photo to the form.
senses.exampleCN: 她把照片附在表格上。
senses.why: Attach comes from Old French atachier, 'to fasten with a nail', so the original act is pinning one object onto another.
senses.whyCN: attach 来自古法语 atachier「用钉子固定」，最初的动作就是把一件东西钉到另一件上。

senses.title: Treat as important
senses.definition: to connect value or importance to something
senses.definitionCN: 把价值或重要性系在某事上
senses.example: The school attaches great importance to reading.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校非常重视阅读。
senses.why: Pinning a value onto a thing is a short step from pinning a label on it, so the physical fastening becomes a judgement of worth.
senses.whyCN: 把价值钉在某物上，与把标签钉在实物上只差一步，于是具体的固定动作变成了对价值的判断。

senses.title: Be emotionally tied
senses.definition: to feel affection that ties you to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 因感情而与某人某物系在一起
senses.example: She is deeply attached to her old bike.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那辆旧自行车很有感情。
senses.why: Affection works like a rope: being attached means the tie is felt rather than seen, ending in the passive form used for fondness.
senses.whyCN: 感情像一根绳：be attached 表示这根绳看不见却能感到，于是被动形式专门用来表示依恋。

intro.en: Attach began as a word about nailing things down and grew senses of value and affection.
intro.cn: attach 起初指用钉子固定，后来长出价值与感情方面的含义。

items.en: tache meant 'a nail or fastening'.
items.cn: tache 意为「钉子、扣件」。

items.en: atachier meant 'to fasten or pin'.
items.cn: atachier 意为「固定、别住」。

items.en: attachen first meant 'to seize legally'.
items.cn: attachen 最初还有「依法扣押」之义。

items.en: The word settled on fastening things together.
items.cn: 词义固定为把东西连接在一起。

items.en: Attach importance to and be attached to developed as fixed uses.
items.cn: 重视与依恋两种说法逐渐固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group is the attach family; the near-meaning group gives verbs of joining.
note.cn: 形近组是 attach 词族；近义组是表示连接的动词。

entries.definition: a thing fastened on
to unfasten
joined or fond of
to fix firmly
to make firm in place
to join together

normalIntro.en: Attach pins one thing to another, and can pin value or feeling too.
normalIntro.cn: attach 把一件东西别到另一件上，也能把价值或感情别上去。

normal.en: The pattern is attach something to something.
normal.cn: 常用结构是 attach something to something。

normal.en: Attach importance to is a formal way to say value.
normal.cn: attach importance to 是「重视」的正式说法。

normal.en: Be attached to usually means feel fond of.
normal.cn: be attached to 通常表示依恋。

normal.en: The double t comes from the prefix and stem meeting.
normal.cn: 双 t 来自前缀与词干相接。

normal.en: The word ends with a ch sound.
normal.cn: 词尾读作 ch 音。

abstract.en: See a paper clip pinning two sheets.
abstract.cn: 想象一个回形针把两页纸别住。

abstract.en: See a price tag tied to a handle.
abstract.cn: 想象价签系在把手上。

abstract.en: See an invisible cord from a hand to an old object.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手与旧物之间有一根看不见的线。

examples.en: She attached a photo to the form.
examples.cn: 她把照片附在表格上。

examples.en: The school attaches great importance to reading.
examples.cn: 这所学校非常重视阅读。

examples.en: She is deeply attached to her old bike.
examples.cn: 她对那辆旧自行车很有感情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 古法语 atachier 是「钉住」：把东西钉在一起是附上；把价值钉在某事上是重视；把感情钉在某人身上是依恋。

root: 源自 Old French atachier「用钉子固定」，词根 tache 意为钉子；由具体的「别住、连上」引申为赋予价值，再引申为情感上的依恋。

sensesIntro.en: A pin, a value and an affection are all things tied to something else.
sensesIntro.cn: 别针、价值与感情，都是系在别的东西上的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pin pushed through two sheets.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根别针穿过两页纸。

branches.en: attach a photo
branches.cn: 附上一张照片

branches.en: attach a label
branches.cn: 系上标签

branches.en: attach importance to
branches.cn: 重视

branches.en: attach no weight to a claim
branches.cn: 不把某种说法当回事

branches.en: be attached to a place
branches.cn: 对某个地方有感情

intro.en: The prefix a- here comes from Latin ad-, and detach reverses the act.
intro.cn: 这里的前缀 a- 来自拉丁语 ad-，而 detach 表示相反的动作。

latinIntro.en: The stem goes back to a Germanic word for a nail, borrowed into French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干可追溯到日耳曼语中表示钉子的词，后被法语借用。

definition_zh: 接触；联系；联络人
definition_en: the state of touching, communication with someone, or a person you can reach
core_image: 两只手在桌面上握到一起
scene: 飞机落地后，她第一时间给家里发了消息。 Please contact me when you arrive.
sceneCN: 这里 contact 指「联系」（第 1 个义项：与人取得沟通）；句意是你到了以后请与我联系。

senses.title: Getting in touch
senses.definition: the act of communicating with someone by message, call or meeting
senses.definitionCN: 通过消息、电话或见面与人沟通的行为
senses.example: We kept in contact after the course ended.
senses.exampleCN: 课程结束后我们仍保持联系。
senses.why: Two people can touch across a city with one short message.
senses.whyCN: 两个人靠一条短信，就能跨过一座城相触。

senses.title: Physical touching
senses.definition: the state of two things or surfaces being in touch
senses.definitionCN: 两个物体或表面相互挨着的状态
senses.example: Wash your hands after contact with the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 接触土壤后要洗手。
senses.why: The oldest sense is still the simplest: two surfaces meet.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项仍然最简单：两个表面碰上了。

senses.title: A person to reach
senses.definition: a person you know who can give help or information
senses.definitionCN: 能提供帮助或信息的熟人
senses.example: She has a contact inside the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 她在部里有一个联络人。
senses.why: A useful name in a notebook is a door that opens later.
senses.whyCN: 笔记本里一个有用的名字，是日后会打开的门。

intro.en: Contact comes from Latin contactus, a touching, from contingere, built on com-, together, and tangere, to touch.
intro.cn: contact 来自拉丁语 contactus（接触），源自动词 contingere，由 com-（一起）与 tangere（触碰）构成。

items.en: Tangere meant to touch or reach a thing.
items.cn: tangere 意为触碰或触及某物。

items.en: Contingere meant to touch together or come into contact.
items.cn: contingere 意为碰到一起或发生接触。

items.en: Contactus named the state of touching.
items.cn: contactus 指相互接触的状态。

items.en: French contact carried the word into social and scientific use.
items.cn: 法语 contact 把这个词带进社交与科学语境。

items.en: English contact first meant physical touching.
items.cn: 英语 contact 最初指身体上的接触。

items.en: Telegraphs and phones added the sense of staying in touch.
items.cn: 电报与电话为它添上了保持联络的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin touch base tact-, and the meaning group names other words for a link between people.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语触碰词基 tact-，近义组列出其他表示人际连接的说法。

entries.definition: a written agreement between two sides
complete and not damaged
relating to the sense of touch
the act of putting a hand on something
the sharing of information between people
a link between people or things

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from two hands meeting on a table, then move to a message crossing a city and to a useful name in a notebook.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从桌面上两只手相握开始，再到一条穿过城市的信息，最后到笔记本里一个有用的名字。

normal.en: Con- is together and tact is touch, so contact is touching together.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，tact 是触碰，contact 就是一起碰上。

normal.en: A handshake is the oldest form of contact.
normal.cn: 握手是最古老的接触方式。

normal.en: A phone call is touch without hands.
normal.cn: 一通电话，是不用手的触碰。

normal.en: Keep the number, and you keep a door.
normal.cn: 留住号码，就留住一扇门。

normal.en: Contact begins where distance ends.
normal.cn: 距离结束的地方，联系就开始了。

abstract.en: Picture two hands meeting across a wooden table.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在木桌上方握到一起。

abstract.en: Picture a name written on the back of a card.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字写在卡片背面。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line drawn between two distant dots.
abstract.cn: 想象两个遥远的点之间画着一条细线。

examples.en: Please contact the office if your plans change.
examples.cn: 如果你的计划有变，请联系办公室。

examples.en: The two wires must not be in contact.
examples.cn: 这两根电线不得接触。

examples.en: He gave me the contact for a good translator.
examples.cn: 他给了我一位好译者的联系方式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 contact 记成 con（一起）加 tact（触碰）：两方碰到一起，无论是手还是消息，都是联系。

root: 源自拉丁语 contactus（接触），动词 contingere 由 com（一起）与 tangere（触碰）构成，本义是碰到一起，后指沟通联系与联络人。

sensesIntro.en: From two surfaces meeting, to voices reaching across a city, and to a name kept for a future need.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两个表面相碰，到声音跨过城市抵达，最后到为日后需要而留下的一个名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands meeting on a table top.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌面之上，两只手相握。

branches.en: The first sense is a message that reaches its person.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是抵达对方的消息。

branches.en: The second sense is the plain meeting of two surfaces.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是两个表面朴素的相碰。

branches.en: The third sense turns the link into a person with a name.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把这条连接变成一个有名字的人。

branches.en: Both senses depend on someone willing to answer.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖一个愿意回应的人。

branches.en: A handshake and a phone call both begin with contact.
branches.cn: 握手与通话都从接触开始。

intro.en: Contact is built on Latin com-, together, plus tangere, to touch, whose participle base is tact-.
intro.cn: contact 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 tangere（触碰）构成，其分词词基为 tact-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin touch base tact- also appears in tactile, tangible and contagious.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的触碰词基 tact- 也出现在 tactile、tangible 与 contagious 中。

items.meaning: a touching together or a link
items.exampleCN: 搬家后他们失去了联系。

items.meaningCN: 无需实体接触即可工作
items.example: She paid with a contactless card.

items.exampleCN: 可以通过电子邮件联系到他。
这个孩子喜欢有触感的玩具。

items.meaning: able to be touched or felt

items.meaning: spreading by touch or near contact
not touched, so whole and undamaged

items.meaning: an agreement drawn tight between sides

definition_zh: 选择；挑选；选集；被选中者
definition_en: the act of choosing someone or something from a group, or the group of chosen items
core_image: 货架前放下的一只小推车，装着被挑出的几件
scene: 评委翻阅完所有报名作品，开始圈定入围名单。 The final selection of paintings will hang in the city hall.
sceneCN: 这里 selection 是「入选作品」（第 4 个义项：被选中的一组东西）；句意是最终入选的画作将悬挂在市政厅。

derivatives.zh: selection 的动词与形容词同根形式，义为「挑选；精选的」
select 加 -ive，义为「有选择性的；挑剔的」

senses.title: The act of choosing
senses.definition: the process of deciding which person or thing to take
senses.definitionCN: 决定取用某人某物的过程
senses.example: Selection of the winner took two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 挑选获胜者花了两个小时。
senses.why: The cart moves slowly along the shelf while choices are made.
senses.whyCN: 推车沿货架缓缓移动，选择正在发生。

senses.title: The range available to choose from
senses.definition: the set of items offered for choosing
senses.definitionCN: 供人挑选的一组东西
senses.example: The menu has a wide selection of dishes.
senses.exampleCN: 菜单提供了丰富的菜品选择。
senses.why: The whole shelf lies open before the cart.
senses.whyCN: 整个货架都摊开在推车面前。

senses.title: Someone or something chosen
senses.definition: the person or item that gets picked
senses.definitionCN: 最终被挑中的那个人或那件物
senses.example: He was the committee's first selection.
senses.exampleCN: 他是委员会的首选之人。
senses.why: One item leaves the shelf and lands in the cart.
senses.whyCN: 一件物品离开货架，落进推车。

senses.title: A group of chosen items
senses.definition: a collection of things chosen from a larger set
senses.definitionCN: 从更大集合中选出的一组
senses.example: This album is a selection of her best songs.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑是她最佳歌曲的选集。
senses.why: The cart rolls away full, leaving the shelf behind.
senses.whyCN: 推车满载离去，货架留在身后。

senses.title: Evolutionary survival of the fittest
senses.definition: the natural process where some organisms survive and reproduce more
senses.definitionCN: 部分生物更易存活繁殖的自然过程
senses.example: Natural selection favors faster animals.
senses.exampleCN: 自然选择偏爱更快的动物。
senses.why: The invisible cart of nature keeps only the strongest items.
senses.whyCN: 自然那只看不见的推车只保留最强的个体。

intro.en: From Latin selectio, the noun of seligere (to pick out).
intro.cn: 来自拉丁语 selectio，即 seligere（挑出）的名词形式。

items.en: The root *leg- again means to gather, the same source as select.
items.cn: 词根 *leg- 同样表「收集」，与 select 同源。

items.en: Selectio means a picking out, formed from seligere with -io.
items.cn: 拉丁语 selectio 由 seligere 加 -io 构成，意为「挑取」。

items.en: Roman writers used selectio for sorting and literary choice.
items.cn: 罗马作家用 selectio 表示整理与文学选材。

items.en: English borrowed selection in the 1500s for acts of choosing.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 selection 表示选择行为。

items.en: Darwin fixed natural selection as a scientific term in 1859.

definition_zh: 对手；反对者；对立的一方
definition_en: a person or side that competes against another in a contest, argues against a proposal, or stands on the other side of a dispute
core_image: 两张长桌从两边同时被推往中间，桌面在中央顶住，谁也无法再前进一寸
scene: 辩论厅的灯全开着，两张长桌面对面摆好，一边的人翻开稿子，另一边的人已经站了起来。 Her main opponent in the debate had prepared for weeks.
sceneCN: 这里的 opponent 是「对手」（第 1 个义项：比赛或辩论中正面对垒的一方）；句意为她在辩论中的主要对手准备了数周。图中可辨识物件：长桌、稿子、站起的人。

pos.zh: 对手；反对者；对立的一方

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 oppositio 而来，词干取自 opponere 的分词，义为「反对；对立面」
由动词 oppose 加 -ing 构成，义为「对立的；相反的」
由 opposition 加 -al 构成，义为「对抗性的；反对派的」

senses.title: A rival in a contest
senses.definition: a person or team that is trying to win the same prize or beat the same record as you
senses.definitionCN: 与你争夺同一个奖项、或试图打破同一纪录的人或队伍
senses.example: She beat her opponent in three straight sets.
senses.exampleCN: 她连下三盘击败了对手。
senses.why: Latin opponere meant to set one thing against another, so a contest puts two people on opposite sides of the same board.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 opponere 意为把一物置于另一物对面，所以一场比赛就是把两个人放在同一块棋盘的两边。

senses.title: A person who argues against something
senses.definition: a person who speaks or votes against a plan, policy or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对某项计划、政策或主张发言反对或投反对票的人
senses.example: The proposal had more opponents than supporters.
senses.exampleCN: 这项提议的反对者比支持者更多。
senses.why: The same verb of setting against works in speech: a view is placed opposite another view, and the person holding it becomes the opponent.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「置于对面」的动词也用于言语：一种主张被摆到另一种主张对面，持这种主张的人就成了反对者。

senses.title: Belonging to the other side
senses.definition: standing on the opposite side in a contest, dispute or armed conflict
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、争端或武装冲突中站在另一边的
senses.example: The opponent army withdrew before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 对方军队在黎明前撤离。
senses.why: Because the word began as a participle meaning the one placed opposite, it could also describe the side itself rather than only a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是分词，意为「被置于对面的那个」，因此它也能形容那一方本身，而不只是某个人。

senses.title: A force or thing working against another
senses.definition: something that pulls, pushes or works in the opposite direction to another thing
senses.definitionCN: 朝相反方向拉扯、推动或运行的事物
senses.example: Each muscle in the arm has an opponent that moves the joint back.
senses.exampleCN: 手臂上每块肌肉都有一块把它反向拉回的对抗肌。
senses.why: The image of two things set against each other extends from people to bodies: whatever pulls one way has a counterpart pulling the other.
senses.whyCN: 两物相互对置的画面从人扩展到身体：凡朝一边拉的，都会有一个朝另一边拉的对应物。

intro.en: Opponent is the Latin participle of a verb meaning to set against, and English took it as a noun for whoever stands opposite; the same verb also gives oppose and opposite.
intro.cn: opponent 是拉丁语中意为「置于对面」的动词的分词形式，英语把它用作名词，指站在对面的那个人；同一动词也给出 oppose 与 opposite。

items.en: The prefix ob- meant toward, against or in the way of, and before p it regularly took the form op-.
items.cn: 前缀 ob- 意为朝向、对着、挡在前方，在 p 之前习惯变为 op-。

items.en: Ponere meant to put or place, and it is the placing verb behind a whole family of English words.
items.cn: ponere 意为放置、摆下，是英语一整族词背后的「放置」动词。

items.en: Ob- plus ponere gave opponere, to set against or place in the way, used of objects, arguments and opponents alike.
items.cn: ob- 与 ponere 合成 opponere，意为置于对面或挡在路前，物件、论点和对手都能用。

items.en: The present participle opponentem named the person doing the setting against, and this form is the direct parent of the English noun.
items.cn: 现在分词 opponentem 指正在「置之于对面」的人，这一形式正是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: Modern English uses opponent for rivals, for those who argue against a plan, for the opposing side, and for anything that pulls the other way.
items.cn: 现代英语用 opponent 指竞争者、反对某项计划的人、对方阵营，以及任何向反方向拉扯的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin verb ponere, which is about placing; the near-meaning group collects other names for the person or side you face.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁动词 ponere（放置）上的词；近义组收其他指「你所面对的人或一方」的名称。

entries.definition: To act or speak against something.
entries.definitionCN: 行动上或言语上反对某事。

entries.definition: The act of resisting, or the side that resists.
entries.definitionCN: 抵抗的行为，或进行抵抗的一方。

entries.definition: Placed facing something else, or as different as possible.

entries.definition: To put forward an idea or question for others to consider.
entries.definitionCN: 把观点或问题提出来供他人考虑。

entries.definition: A person competing for the same goal as another.
entries.definitionCN: 为同一目标与他人竞争的人。

entries.definition: A person or group on the other side of a conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 冲突中站在另一边的人或群体。

entries.definition: A person or firm trying to do better than others.
entries.definitionCN: 力图胜过他人的个人或公司。

entries.definition: An enemy in battle or in a long quarrel.
entries.definitionCN: 战斗或长期争斗中的敌人。

normalIntro.en: Opponent is a Latin participle doing noun work, so the hooks keep the picture of something placed directly opposite something else.
normalIntro.cn: opponent 是拉丁语分词在充当名词，所以记忆钩子始终保留「一物被摆在另一物正对面」的画面。

normal.en: Opponent is the participle of opponere, the one set against, so the ending marks a person in the middle of the action.
normal.cn: opponent 是 opponere 的分词，指被置于对面的那个人，词尾标出的正是一个身处动作中的人。

normal.en: The prefix is ob- before p, which is why opponent looks like oppose but not like obvious.
normal.cn: 前缀是 p 前的 ob-，所以 opponent 与 oppose 相像，却与 obvious 不同。

normal.en: Opposition comes from the same verb through its participle stem opposit-, so the pair keeps one root.
normal.cn: opposition 经由分词词干 opposit- 出自同一动词，两者共用一个词根。

normal.en: The hand has an opponens muscle that pulls the thumb across the palm, literally setting it against the fingers.
normal.cn: 手部有一块对掌肌，名字直译就是把拇指移到手指对面，正是「置于对面」的本义。

normal.en: In a debate, an opponent faces you; on the battlefield, the opponent army faces yours, and the word fits both.
normal.cn: 辩论时对手正面朝你；战场上对方军队正对你的军队，这个词两处都合用。

abstract.en: A word for the person opposite reminds us that a contest is always a pair, never one side alone.
abstract.cn: 指「对面那个人」的词提醒我们：一场较量总是成双的，从不只有一边。

abstract.en: Setting something against something else is how arguments begin, and the word does not say who is right.
abstract.cn: 把一物置于另一物对面，正是争论的开始，而这个词并不判定谁对。

abstract.en: Even inside the body, every pull has a counter-pull, and English borrowed the same noun for that quiet balance.
abstract.cn: 即便在身体里，每一次牵拉都有反向牵拉，英语也用同一个名词来指这份沉默的平衡。

examples.en: She beat her opponent in three straight sets.
examples.cn: 她连下三盘击败了对手。

examples.en: The proposal had more opponents than supporters.
examples.cn: 这项提议的反对者比支持者更多。

examples.en: Each muscle has an opponent that pulls the joint back.
examples.cn: 每块肌肉都有一块把关节反向拉回的对抗肌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偶碰能」——两人偶一碰上，就得比一比谁能站稳；记住 opponent 是对手。

root: 来自拉丁语 opponere（置于对面）的现在分词 opponentem，由 ob-（朝向、对着，在 p 前变 op-）与 ponere（放置）合成。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one thing placed against another; from that face-to-face position come the rival, the person who argues back, the opposing side and the counter-pull in a body.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一物被置于另一物对面；从这个正面对峙的位置分出竞争者、出言反对的人、对方阵营，以及身体里的反向牵拉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two long tables pushed from opposite sides until they meet and neither can move further.
core.cn: 核心意象：两张长桌从两边同时被推往中间，桌面在中央顶住，谁也无法再前进一寸。

branches.en: two players waiting on opposite sides of a net
branches.cn: 球网两边各自等着的两个球员

branches.en: a hall where a proposal is spoken against
branches.cn: 提案被人出言反对的大厅

branches.en: a column advancing toward another column
branches.cn: 朝另一支队伍推进的队伍

branches.en: a muscle pulling a joint back the other way
branches.cn: 把关节反向拉回的肌肉

branches.en: the same word for the body opposite and the voice against
branches.cn: 同一个词，兼指对面的身体与反对的声音

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix of opposition plus the verb for placing, worn into a participle; English adds noun and adjectival endings from there.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「对着」的拉丁前缀与「放置」动词合成、再磨成分词；英语由此再接名词与形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere, opponere and oppositio are recorded, so this family has a reliable Latin ancestry and a clear image of placing one thing against another.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ponere、opponere、oppositio 均有记录，因此这一族英语词有可靠的拉丁语世系，也有清晰的「把一物置于另一物对面」的画面。

senses.title: Reading aloud: the act of reading
senses.definition: the act of reading a text, especially aloud and in a formal setting (now archaic)
senses.definitionCN: 阅读文本的行为，尤指在正式场合朗读（现已古旧）
senses.example: In the monastery the lecture of the psalm began at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 修道院里，晨祷时对圣咏的诵读从黎明开始。
senses.why: Lecture came from Medieval Latin lectura, 'a reading'. Before it named a talk, it named the act of reading itself, and the oldest English examples keep that plain sense.
senses.whyCN: lecture 来自中世纪拉丁语 lectura“阅读”。在它指“讲座”之前，它指的就是“读”这个行为，最早的英语用例保留着这层朴素含义。

senses.title: A formal talk that teaches
senses.titleCN: 讲座：面向听众的正式讲授
senses.definition: a formal talk given to a group of people, especially students, in order to teach or inform them
senses.definitionCN: 为教授或告知一群人（尤指学生）而作的正式讲话
senses.example: She went to a lecture on the history of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 她去听了一场关于这座城市历史的讲座。
senses.why: In the 16c a lecture was a discourse read or delivered before an audience. The act of reading aloud turned into the public teaching talk, which is now the central sense.
senses.whyCN: 在 16 世纪，lecture 指向听众读出或讲出的一段论述。“朗读”这个动作由此变成公开的教学讲话，也就是今天最核心的义项。

senses.title: A course unit: one class in a series
senses.titleCN: 课时：课程中的一个讲授单元
senses.definition: a single period of instruction in a course, or the course seen as a series of such talks
senses.definitionCN: 课程中的一节讲授，或由一系列讲授构成的整门课
senses.example: The course consists of twelve lectures and four seminars.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课由十二次讲授和四次研讨课组成。
senses.why: Once a lecture is put on a timetable, the talk becomes the unit of a course. Attendance is counted in lectures, and the syllabus is divided into them.
senses.whyCN: 一旦讲座被排进课表，这场讲话就成了课程的计量单位。出勤按“讲”计算，教学大纲也按讲次划分。

senses.title: The written text of a talk
senses.titleCN: 讲稿：写在纸上的那份讲授
senses.definition: the written text or full notes from which a talk is delivered, or a published version of it
senses.definitionCN: 演讲所依据的书面文本或完整讲稿，也指其出版形式
senses.example: She wrote out the lecture in full before rehearsing it.
senses.exampleCN: 她先把讲稿完整写出来，再开始排练。
senses.why: A talk can be fixed on paper before or after it is spoken. The same noun then names the script the speaker holds, which is why one can write, revise or print a lecture.
senses.whyCN: 讲话在说之前或之后都可以固定在纸上。同一个名词于是也指讲者手里的稿子，所以说“写讲稿、改讲稿、印讲稿”都成立。

senses.title: A serious scolding
senses.definition: a long, serious talk to someone about their behaviour, given as a warning or punishment
senses.definitionCN: 就某人的行为作长时间严肃谈话，作为警告或惩罚
senses.example: His father gave him a lecture about wasting money.
senses.exampleCN: 父亲就乱花钱的事训了他一顿。
senses.why: The instructive frame is now aimed at correction. The content is still teaching, but the listener is being told off, so praise and warning replace neutral explanation.
senses.whyCN: 讲授的框架这时对准了“纠正”：内容仍是在教，但听者是在挨批评，于是中性的讲解换成了告诫与责难。

senses.title: Verb: teach by giving talks
senses.definition: to give a formal talk to students or to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 给学生或听众作正式讲授
senses.example: Professor Lin lectures on constitutional history.
senses.exampleCN: 林教授讲授宪政史。
senses.why: This is zero derivation: the noun became a verb with no added suffix, naming the activity of the person behind the lectern.
senses.whyCN: 这是零派生：名词不加任何后缀直接变成动词，指讲台后面那个人所做的事。

senses.title: Verb: scold at length
senses.definition: to talk seriously and at length to someone about something they have done wrong
senses.definitionCN: 就某人做错的事进行长时间严肃谈话
senses.example: The coach lectured the team for giving up in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 教练因球队下半场放弃而训了他们一顿。
senses.why: The verb takes the corrective branch too. Now it has a target and a fault, and the length of the talk is part of the reproach.
senses.whyCN: 动词也接上了“纠正”这一支：此时它带有对象和过错，而“讲得很长”本身就是责难的一部分。

senses.title: A public lecture as an event
senses.titleCN: 公开讲座：作为活动的讲演
senses.definition: a public talk organized as an event, often by a university, museum or learned society
senses.definitionCN: 作为活动组织的公开演讲，常由大学、博物馆或学术团体举办
senses.example: The museum's annual lecture drew an audience of five hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的年度讲座吸引了五百名听众。
senses.why: The form spreads beyond the classroom. A lecture can now be an event with a title, a guest speaker and tickets, even when no course is involved.
senses.whyCN: 这种形式走出了课堂。lecture 现在可以是一场有标题、有嘉宾讲者、需要门票的活动，即使并不附属于任何课程。

intro.en: Lecture is a reading word before it is a teaching word. Latin legere 'to read' goes back to 'pick out, gather', and English first used lecture for the act of reading, then for the talk.
intro.cn: lecture 先是“阅读”词，后来才是“教学”词。拉丁语 legere“读”的本义是“拣出、采集”；英语先用它指阅读行为，再指讲授。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'the act of reading, a reading aloud', borrowed from Medieval Latin lectura.
items.cn: 最早记录于 14 世纪晚期的英语，意为“阅读行为、朗读”，借自中世纪拉丁语 lectura。

items.en: lectura 'a reading' is a noun of action from lectus, the past participle of legere 'to read'.
items.cn: lectura“阅读”是由 legere“读”的过去分词 lectus 构成的行为名词。

items.en: legere meant 'to read', but its older sense was 'to pick out, select, gather'. Reading is pictured as picking out letters one by one from the page.
items.cn: legere 意为“读”，更早的意思是“拣出、挑选、采集”。阅读被想象成从页面上把字母一个个拣出来。

items.en: legere is traced to PIE *leg- 'to collect, gather, pick out'. The step from 'gather' to 'read' is inferred rather than attested, so this deeper link is generally accepted.
items.cn: legere 被追溯到原始印欧语 *leg-“收集、采集、拣出”。从“采集”到“读”这一步是推论而非有据可查，因此这层更深的联系属于一般认为是。

items.en: The sense 'a discourse read or delivered before an audience' appears in the 16c. By the 17c lecture is the ordinary word for a university talk, and the old 'reading' sense fades.
items.cn: “向听众读出或讲出的一段论述”这一义项见于 16 世纪。到 17 世纪，lecture 已是大学讲课的常用词，旧的“阅读”义逐渐退场。

items.en: Lecture and legal are not the same family: legere is the verb 'to read', while lex (genitive legis) is the noun 'law'. Both contain the leg- shape and are traced to *leg- 'gather', but law is not a form of 'read'.
items.cn: lecture 与 legal 并非同一家族：legere 是动词“读”，lex（属格 legis）是名词“法”。两者都含 leg- 这一形，都被追溯到 *leg-“采集”，但“法”并不是“读”的某种形式。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the reading root legere from the law noun lex. The near-meaning group separates a teaching talk from other kinds of public speech.
note.cn: 形近组把“读”的词根 legere 与“法”的名词 lex 分开；近义组把教学性讲授与其他类型的公开讲话分开。

entries.definition: a stand for a book or notes, used by someone who is reading or speaking. It comes from the same legere 'read' family, not from lecture itself.
entries.definitionCN: 供朗读或演讲者放置书本、讲稿的架子。它出自同一个 legere“读”的词族，而不是由 lecture 派生。

entries.definition: clear enough to be read. It is legere plus -ibilis 'able to be', so it describes writing that can be read, not a talk that is given.
entries.definitionCN: 字迹清楚、可辨认的。它是 legere 加 -ibilis“能够被……”，形容文字可读，而不是形容所作的讲座。

entries.definition: the body that makes laws. It looks as if it contains lecture's root, but it is lex 'law' plus lator 'proposer', so the meaning is law-making, not reading.
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关。它看起来含有 lecture 的词根，其实是 lex“法”加 lator“提出者”，所以意思是立法，而不是阅读。

entries.definition: a formal address to an audience. It is broader than lecture and need not teach anything; a lecture is expected to inform.
entries.definitionCN: 面向听众的正式讲话。它比 lecture 宽泛，不必包含教学；而 lecture 默认要传递知识。

entries.definition: a class in which a small group discusses a topic. It is interactive and smaller, while a lecture is one voice addressing many.
entries.definitionCN: 小组讨论某个主题的课程。它强调互动且人数少，而 lecture 是一个声音对许多人讲。

entries.definition: a talk on a religious or moral theme, usually delivered in worship. It aims at the conscience, not at course content.
entries.definitionCN: 关于宗教或道德主题的讲话，通常在礼拜中宣讲。它对准的是良知，而不是课程内容。

entries.definition: a formal or official rebuke. It is usually shorter and more procedural than a lecture, which explains and moralizes at length.
entries.definitionCN: 正式或官方的斥责。它通常比 lecture 短、更讲程序，而 lecture 会长篇解释并说教。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: legere 'read', its past participle lectus, and the English family lectern, legible, legend and lesson.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：legere“读”、它的过去分词 lectus，以及英语中的 lectern、legible、legend、lesson。

normal.en: legere 'to read' gives the lect- stem; lecture is literally 'a reading' before it is a talk.
normal.cn: legere“读”给出 lect- 这个词干；lecture 字面上就是“一次阅读”，之后才成为“讲座”。

normal.en: lectern, legible, legend and lesson all come from the same 'read / pick out' family, so the reading image is still visible around lecture.
normal.cn: lectern、legible、legend、lesson 都出自同一个“读／拣出”词族，因此“阅读”的意象在 lecture 周围仍然看得见。

normal.en: The old sense 'a reading' explains why a lecture was once something read aloud rather than freely spoken.
normal.cn: 古义“一次阅读”解释了为什么 lecture 早先是“朗读出来的东西”，而不是即兴讲话。

normal.en: lecture notes and lecture hall keep the classroom frame: notes record the talk, the hall houses it.
normal.cn: lecture notes 与 lecture hall 保留着课堂框架：笔记记录讲授，讲堂容纳讲授。

normal.en: give somebody a lecture moves the same talk from teaching to correcting, which is why the verb can mean 'scold'.
normal.cn: give somebody a lecture 把同一场讲话从“教”移到“纠正”，所以动词可以表示“训斥”。

abstract.en: Picture a page under a lamp: letters are picked out one by one, then the same words are spoken to rows of listeners. Lecture is that page becoming a voice.
abstract.cn: 想象台灯下的一页纸：字母被一个个拣出来，随后同一串词被念给一排排听众。lecture 就是那页纸变成声音的过程。

abstract.en: The voice can teach or scold; only the listener's posture changes — a notebook open, or a head held down.
abstract.cn: 同一个声音可以教人，也可以训人；变的只是听者的姿态——要么摊开笔记本，要么低着头。

abstract.en: A lecture is a text that has learned to stand up and speak, and a course is a row of such texts standing in line.
abstract.cn: 一场 lecture 是一段学会站起来说话的文字，而一门课程就是这样的文字排成一列。

examples.en: The lecture on volcanoes was full of photographs from the 1980 eruption.
examples.cn: 那场关于火山的讲座满是 1980 年喷发的照片。

examples.en: He lectures to first-year students three mornings a week.
examples.cn: 他每周有三个上午给一年级学生授课。

examples.en: My mother lectured me for twenty minutes about the unpaid bill.
examples.cn: 母亲为那张没付的账单训了我二十分钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: “来课扯”——上课时把内容扯成一大段 → lecture 讲座、训斥

root: 拉丁语 legere“读”（本义“采集、挑选”）→ 中世纪拉丁 lectura“阅读”，核心是“把文字拣出来、念给人听”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of lecture, one movement: a text is picked out and read, the reading becomes a talk, the talk becomes a course unit and a script, and finally the same instructive voice turns into a scolding.
sensesIntro.cn: lecture 的八个义项是一条运动线：文字被拣出来读，读变成讲授，讲授变成课时与讲稿，最后同一种“教导口吻”变成训斥。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words are picked out of a page and spoken to people who came to listen.
core.cn: 核心意象：把字从纸页上拣出来，念给前来听的人。

branches.en: READING: the oldest layer, when lecture names the act of reading rather than a talk.
branches.cn: 阅读：最古老的一层，此时 lecture 指的是“读”这一行为，而不是讲座。

branches.en: INSTRUCTION: the classroom talk, the verb for giving it, and the public lecture as an event.
branches.cn: 讲授：课堂讲座、表示“讲授”的动词，以及作为活动的公开讲座。

branches.en: COURSE UNIT: the talk becomes a countable slot in a timetable and a syllabus.
branches.cn: 课时：讲座变成课表与教学大纲里可计数的一格。

branches.en: WRITTEN TEXT: the spoken words are fixed on paper as a script or a printed talk.
branches.cn: 书面文本：说出的话被固定在纸上，成为讲稿或印行的讲辞。

branches.en: CORRECTION: the instructive voice turns into a long scolding, as a noun and as a verb.
branches.cn: 纠正：教导的口吻变成长篇训斥，名词与动词都走这一支。

intro.en: Lecture is a borrowed Latin noun, not a prefixed English word. English adds only ordinary suffixes: -er for the person, -ship for the post, -ing for the activity; the noun also became a verb with no suffix at all.
intro.cn: lecture 是借入的拉丁名词，不是由英语前缀构成的词。英语只加普通后缀：-er 表人，-ship 表职位，-ing 表活动；名词还零派生成了动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base legere 'read / pick out' has a large family. Note that lex 'law' is a different noun with a similar shape, and legare 'send, bequeath' is a different verb again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 legere“读／拣出”有一个很大的词族。注意 lex“法”是形似的另一个名词，legare“派出、遗赠”又是另一个动词。

items.meaning: a person who gives lectures, especially at a university
items.meaningCN: 讲师；授课者（-er 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The lecturer paused to answer a question.
items.exampleCN: 讲师停下来回答了一个问题。

items.meaning: the post or position of a lecturer
items.meaningCN: 讲师职位；讲席（-ship 表示职位或身份）
items.example: She was appointed to a lectureship in physics.
items.exampleCN: 她获聘物理学讲师职位。

items.meaningCN: 授课；讲学（-ing 构成行为名词）
items.example: His lecturing took him to six countries.
items.exampleCN: 他的讲学让他去了六个国家。

items.meaning: to give a lecture; to scold at length
items.meaningCN: 讲授；长篇训斥（名动同形，不加后缀）

items.meaning: to read; to pick out, gather
items.example: The verb is the root shared by lecture, lector and collect.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 lecture、lector、collect 共有的词根。

items.example: Every English word on this stem keeps the reading image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干上的英语词都保留“读”的意象。

items.example: It turns the act of reading into the noun lecture.
items.exampleCN: 它把“读”的动作变成名词 lecture。

items.meaning: a reader; one who reads aloud in a service
items.meaningCN: 诵读者；（礼拜中的）读经员
items.example: The lector read the passage aloud to the congregation.
items.exampleCN: 读经员向会众朗读了那段经文。

items.structure: Medieval Latin lectrum, from the stem lect-
items.meaning: a reading desk, especially in a church
items.example: She set her notes on the lectern before speaking.
items.exampleCN: 发言前她把讲稿放在讲台上。

latinEntries.meaning: able to be read; clear enough to read
latinEntries.meaningCN: 可读的；字迹清晰的（-ibilis 表“能够被……”）

latinEntries.meaning: a story handed down; originally 'things to be read' about the saints
latinEntries.meaningCN: 传说；原指关于圣徒“应被诵读的事迹”

latinEntries.meaning: a unit of teaching; originally a passage read aloud
latinEntries.meaningCN: 课；原义是“所读的一段文字”

latinEntries.meaning: to bring things together; literally 'to gather up'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 收集；字面义“把东西拣到一起”

definition_zh: 生的；未加工的；生疏的；裸露刺痛的
definition_en: not cooked; not processed or refined; inexperienced and untrained; bare and sore, of skin or nerves
core_image: 刚出矿的粗糙石块，棱角上还粘着砂粒
scene: 采石场里，刚开采出的石块粗糙发灰，棱角上还粘着砂粒。 The raw material is shipped to the factory for processing.
sceneCN: 这里 raw 是「未加工的」（第 2 个义项：尚未经过处理或提炼）；句意为原材料被运往工厂加工。画面里可留意：粗糙的石块、棱角的砂粒、运石的车。

pos.zh: 生的；未加工的；生疏的；裸露刺痛的

derivatives.zh: raw 加 -ness，指生、未加工的状态
raw 加 -ly，指生硬地、赤裸地
raw 与 hide 复合，指生皮

senses.title: Not cooked
senses.definition: of food, not cooked at all
senses.definitionCN: 指食物完全没有烹煮
senses.example: Cats can eat raw meat.
senses.exampleCN: 猫可以吃生肉。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply uncooked, and it still describes food taken straight from the fireless kitchen.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是「未煮」，至今仍用来描述未经火候的食物。

senses.title: Not processed
senses.definition: of a material, not yet treated, refined or manufactured
senses.definitionCN: 指材料尚未经过处理、提炼或制造
senses.example: The raw material is shipped to the factory.
senses.exampleCN: 原材料被运往工厂。
senses.why: From uncooked food the word extended to any material that has not yet been worked into its final form.
senses.whyCN: 从「未煮的食物」扩展到任何尚未被加工成最终形态的材料。

senses.title: Inexperienced
senses.definition: new to something and not yet trained or hardened
senses.definitionCN: 刚接触某事、尚未训练或磨练的
senses.example: The raw recruits were still learning to march.
senses.exampleCN: 新兵们还在学习列队行进。
senses.why: A person who has not been through training is like material not yet worked, so raw came to mean inexperienced.
senses.whyCN: 未经训练的人就像尚未加工的材料，于是 raw 引申为「生疏」。

senses.title: Bare and sore
senses.definition: of skin or a nerve, exposed and painful, without protection
senses.definitionCN: 指皮肤或神经外露、疼痛、缺乏保护
senses.example: The cold wind stung his raw face.
senses.exampleCN: 寒风刺着他裸露发疼的脸。
senses.why: Skin stripped of its covering is exposed like unworked material, and the painful openness gave the word its sense of soreness.
senses.whyCN: 失去覆盖的皮肤就像未经处理的材料一样暴露在外，这种疼痛的暴露给了这个词「刺痛」的意思。

intro.en: Raw is a native English word from Old English hreaw, meaning uncooked, with relatives in other Germanic languages; no Latin source is recorded.
intro.cn: raw 是英语本族词，来自古英语 hreaw（未煮的），在其他日耳曼语言中有亲属词；没有拉丁语来源记录。

items.en: Hreaw meant uncooked or unprocessed, and it described food and materials alike.
items.cn: hreaw 意为未煮或未加工的，既形容食物，也形容材料。

items.en: Related forms in other Germanic languages carry the same sense of something not yet cooked or worked.
items.cn: 其他日耳曼语言中的相关形式带有同样的「尚未煮或加工」之意。

items.en: Middle English raw kept the sense of uncooked and extended it to what was rough and unfinished.
items.cn: 中古英语 raw 保留「未煮」的意思，并扩展到粗糙、未完成之物。

items.en: Because what is unworked is also untrained or uncovered, raw came to describe new soldiers and bare skin.
items.cn: 由于未加工之物也意味着未受训练或未被覆盖，raw 便用来形容新兵与裸露的皮肤。

items.en: Modern English uses raw for uncooked food, unprocessed material, inexperienced people, and exposed flesh.
items.cn: 现代英语用 raw 指生食、未加工的材料、无经验的人，以及裸露的皮肉。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and one easily confused word; the near-meaning group gathers words for the uncooked, the unrefined and the untrained.
note.cn: 形近组收复合词与一个易混词；近义组收表示生的、未精炼的、未受训练的词。

entries.definition: The state of being raw.
Untreated leather made from hide.
entries.definitionCN: 用生皮制成的未处理皮革。

entries.definition: Thin with large bones.
Lightly cooked, easily confused with raw.
entries.definitionCN: 半熟的，容易与 raw 混淆。

entries.definition: Not prepared with heat.
In a natural state, not refined.
entries.definitionCN: 处于自然状态、未经精炼的。

entries.definition: Not treated by an industrial process.
New to an activity, without practice.

normalIntro.en: The word begins as uncooked, then covers unworked material, untrained people and unprotected skin, all sharing the idea of not yet finished.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「未煮」开始，随后覆盖未加工的材料、未受训练的人与未受保护的皮肤，都共享「尚未完成」这一想法。

normal.en: Raw and rare are close in the kitchen, but raw is completely uncooked while rare is lightly cooked.
normal.cn: 在厨房里 raw 与 rare 相近，但 raw 是完全没煮，rare 是略煮。

normal.en: Raw material is what a factory turns into a finished product.
normal.cn: raw material 是工厂加工成成品之前的材料。

normal.en: Raw data has not yet been cleaned or sorted.
normal.cn: raw data 是尚未清理或整理的数据。

normal.en: A raw recruit is a soldier who has not yet been trained.
normal.cn: raw recruit 是尚未受过训练的新兵。

normal.en: Raw skin is skin stripped of its covering and left sore.
normal.cn: raw skin 是失去覆盖、裸露发疼的皮肤。

abstract.en: What is raw is full of possibility but not yet usable.
abstract.cn: raw 之物充满可能，却尚不可用。

abstract.en: To be raw is to be honest and exposed at the same time.
abstract.cn: raw 既是坦诚，也是暴露。

abstract.en: Every finished thing once lay raw and unshaped.
abstract.cn: 每一件成品都曾经是未成形的原材料。

examples.en: Cats can eat raw meat.
examples.cn: 猫可以吃生肉。

examples.en: The raw material is shipped to the factory for processing.
examples.cn: 原材料被运往工厂加工。

examples.en: The raw recruits were still learning to march.
examples.cn: 新兵们还在学习列队行进。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「刚从矿里挖出的石块」——粗糙、没加工过，记住 raw 是生的、未加工的。

root: 古英语 hreaw（未煮的）→ 中古英语 raw → 现代英语 raw；同族有 rawness、rawhide、rawboned。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is not yet finished; the senses divide into uncooked food, unprocessed material, untrained people, and unprotected skin.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「尚未完成」；义项分为未煮的食物、未加工的材料、未受训练的人，以及未受保护的皮肤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough stone just cut from the quarry, grit still clinging to its edges.
core.cn: 核心意象：刚从采石场切下的粗糙石块，棱角上还粘着砂粒。

branches.en: meat straight from the fireless kitchen
branches.cn: 未经火候的生肉

branches.en: ore and stone at the quarry face
branches.cn: 采石场工作面上的矿石与石块

branches.en: a recruit still learning to march
branches.cn: 还在学习列队的新兵

branches.en: skin stripped bare by the wind

branches.en: unworked material and untrained people
branches.cn: 未加工的材料与未受训练的人

definition_zh: 螺丝；拧；螺旋；搞砸
definition_en: a metal pin with a spiral ridge, to turn it into place, a spiral form, or to ruin something in informal use
core_image: 螺丝刀把一枚螺丝一点点拧进木板，木屑从螺纹间挤出
scene: 他用螺丝刀把螺丝拧进木板。 He drove the screw into the wood with a screwdriver.
sceneCN: 这里 screw 是「螺丝」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他用螺丝刀把螺丝拧进木板。

senses.title: A spiral fastener
senses.definition: a metal pin with a spiral ridge, used to join things
senses.definitionCN: 带螺旋纹、用于连接物体的金属钉
senses.example: Tighten the screw with a screwdriver.
senses.exampleCN: 用螺丝刀把螺丝拧紧。
senses.why: The core sense is the fastening object.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是紧固物件。

senses.title: To turn into place
senses.definition: to turn a screw or lid so that it goes in or comes off
senses.definitionCN: 旋转螺丝或盖子使其进入或脱开
senses.example: He screwed the lid onto the jar.
senses.exampleCN: 他把盖子拧到罐子上。
senses.why: The object's use becomes the action.
senses.whyCN: 物件的用途变成动作。

senses.title: A spiral form
senses.definition: a shape that winds around like a screw thread
senses.definitionCN: 像螺纹一样盘绕的形状
senses.example: The staircase winds in a screw.
senses.exampleCN: 楼梯呈螺旋形盘旋。
senses.why: The shape that lets a screw grip becomes a general form.
senses.whyCN: 让螺丝咬合的形态成为一种普遍形状。

senses.title: To ruin or cheat
senses.definition: to ruin something, or to cheat someone, in informal use

senses.example: He screwed the deal by arriving late.
senses.exampleCN: 他因迟到把交易搞砸了。
senses.why: A twisted thread becomes an image of things going wrong.
senses.whyCN: 扭曲的螺纹成为事情出错的意象。

intro.cn: screw 可能源自古法语 escroue（螺母、螺丝），也许来自拉丁语 scrofa（母猪）。

items.en: Scrofa meant a sow, perhaps because of the curled shape.
items.cn: scrofa 意为母猪，可能因卷曲形状而得名。

items.en: Escroue meant a nut or a screw.
items.cn: escroue 意为螺母或螺丝。

items.en: Screw named a spiral fastening device.
items.cn: screw 指螺旋紧固装置。

items.en: Screw also meant to turn something into place.

items.en: Screw has informal senses of ruining or cheating.
items.cn: 现代英语中 screw 有搞砸或欺骗的非正式义。

note.en: Screw is compared with similar-looking words and with words for fasteners and turning.
note.cn: 把 screw 与形近词以及表示紧固件和旋转的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: A screw is a spiral fastener, and to screw is to turn it.
normalIntro.cn: screw 是螺旋紧固件，to screw 就是旋转它。

normal.en: A screwdriver turns a screw.
normal.cn: 螺丝刀转动螺丝。

abstract.en: A spiral turns forward motion into grip.

abstract.en: The same turning motion can fix or destroy.

abstract.en: The tool and its shape share one short word.

examples.en: Tighten the screw with a screwdriver.
examples.cn: 用螺丝刀把螺丝拧紧。

sensesIntro.cn: screw 意为螺丝、拧紧、螺旋，或非正式地搞砸。

branches.cn: 金属紧固件本身。

definition_zh: 结果；结局；成果；结局指标
definition_en: the result or final situation produced by an event, process, decision, or treatment
core_image: 一条路走到尽头，终点处落下一个清晰的印记
scene: 临床试验结束时，研究团队把两组康复率并排写进同一张表。 The main outcome was clear: the treated group recovered twelve points more often than the control group.
sceneCN: 这里 outcome 是“（研究或临床的）结局指标”（第 8 个义项：统计意义上的终点指标）；句意：主要结局指标很清楚：用药组的康复率比对照组高出十二个百分点。图中可辨识物件：病历表、统计柱状图、药瓶、研究记录；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 即将到来的；乐于提供信息的

senses.title: The result of an event or process
senses.definition: the result or final situation that follows from an event or process
senses.definitionCN: 由某个事件或过程产生的最终结果或局面
senses.example: The outcome of the experiment surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 实验的结果让所有人都感到意外。
senses.why: The word is a compound of out and come: something comes out of a process and stands at the end of it. The result is pictured as a thing that emerges and becomes visible once the process is finished.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 out 与 come 复合而成：某物从过程里“走出来”，停在过程的末端。结果被想象成一件在过程结束后浮现、变得可见的东西。

senses.title: A consequence of a decision
senses.definition: the effect that a decision or action has, often considered before it is made
senses.definitionCN: 某个决定或行动带来的效果，常在做出决定前就被考虑
senses.example: Before you speak, consider the outcome of your words.
senses.exampleCN: 开口之前，先想想你的话会带来什么后果。
senses.why: The same emergence is now read backwards as consequence: the decision sends something out, and that something returns as the situation you must live in.
senses.whyCN: 同样的“浮现”现在被反向读成后果：决定送出某样东西，而那样东西又作为你必须生活在其中的局面返回。

senses.title: The result of a contest or vote
senses.definition: the final result of an election, trial, game, or negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 选举、审判、比赛或谈判的最终结果
senses.example: The outcome of the election remained unclear for days.
senses.exampleCN: 选举结果数日未明。
senses.why: A contest is a process with a single end point, so outcome fits it naturally. The word does not say who won; it names the shape the whole process leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 竞赛是一个有单一终点的过程，因此 outcome 天然适用。这个词不说明谁赢，只命名整个过程留下的那个形状。

senses.title: A medical or clinical result
senses.definition: the health result of a treatment or illness for a patient or group
senses.definitionCN: 治疗或疾病给患者或群体带来的健康结果
senses.example: Better hygiene led to improved patient outcomes.
senses.exampleCN: 更好的卫生条件改善了患者的治疗结果。
senses.why: Medicine turns the everyday word into a measured endpoint: the process is treatment, and what comes out at the end is the patient's condition. The metaphor of emergence becomes a chart.
senses.whyCN: 医学把日常词变成可测量的终点：过程是治疗，末端“走出来”的是患者的状况。浮现的比喻变成了一张图表。

senses.title: The expected or desired result
senses.definition: the result that people hope for or predict, often stated in advance
senses.definitionCN: 人们希望或预测的结果，常被提前说明
senses.example: The negotiators aimed for a fair outcome for both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判者力求让双方都得到公平的结果。
senses.why: Once the end point is known to be a result, it can be wished for before it exists. The word stops describing what happened and starts naming a target placed at the end of the process.
senses.whyCN: 一旦知道末端是一个结果，它就可以在存在之前被期盼。这个词于是不再描述已发生的事，而是命名一个被放在过程末端的目标。

senses.title: A learning outcome in education
senses.definition: a specific skill or understanding that students are expected to gain from a course
senses.definitionCN: 学生预期从课程中获得的具体技能或理解
senses.example: Each lesson lists three learning outcomes.
senses.exampleCN: 每节课都列出三项学习成果。
senses.why: Education reverses the direction: instead of asking what came out of teaching, it first declares what should come out. The outcome becomes a designed destination rather than a report.
senses.whyCN: 教育把方向倒过来：不是问教学之后“出来了什么”，而是先声明“应该出来什么”。结果由事后报告变成事先设计的目的地。

senses.title: The result of a legal case
senses.definition: the final decision or settlement of a legal dispute or court case
senses.definitionCN: 法律争议或法庭案件的最终裁决或和解
senses.example: The case outcome depended on one witness.
senses.exampleCN: 案件结果取决于一名证人。
senses.why: A trial is a bounded procedure with an official end, so its result is called an outcome rather than a mere effect. The word suits any process that is formally closed.
senses.whyCN: 审判是一个有官方终点的有限程序，因此它的结果被称为 outcome，而不只是 effect。这个词适用于任何正式结束的过程。

senses.title: A measured endpoint in research
senses.definition: a variable that researchers measure at the end of a study to judge whether an intervention worked
senses.definitionCN: 研究者在研究结束时测量、用来判断干预是否有效的变量
senses.example: Recovery rate was the primary outcome of the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 康复率是该试验的主要终点指标。
senses.why: Statistics narrows outcome to one measured thing among many possible results. The end of the process is now a designated variable, chosen before the data are collected so the question cannot be moved afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把 outcome 收窄为众多可能结果中被选定测量的一项。过程的末端现在是一个事先指定的变量，在收集数据前就定好，以免事后移动问题。

intro.en: Outcome is not Latin at all. It is a Scottish English compound of two native words, and its history shows the modern sense is surprisingly late.
intro.cn: outcome 根本不是拉丁词。它是两个英语本族词构成的苏格兰英语复合词，其历史显示现代义出现得相当晚。

items.en: c. 1200, out-coming was used for 'an emergence, act or fact of coming out'. Old English had utancumen 'stranger, foreigner', literally 'one who came from outside'.
items.cn: 约 1200 年，out-coming 表示“出现、出来的行为或事实”。古英语有 utancumen“陌生人、外来者”，字面是“从外面来的人”。

items.en: The noun outcome is recorded in 1788, originally Scottish, meaning 'that which results from something'. It comes from the verbal phrase out + come.
items.cn: 名词 outcome 记录于 1788 年，最初见于苏格兰，义为“由某事物产生的结果”。它来自动词短语 out + come。

items.en: Popularized in English by Thomas Carlyle around the 1830s, according to standard references.
items.cn: 据通行资料，托马斯·卡莱尔在 1830 年代前后使这个词在英语中流行开来。

items.en: The word stays a transparent compound: out (forth, into view) + come (arrive). Its force is that the result is something that came out and can now be seen.
items.cn: 这个词始终是透明的复合词：out（向外、进入视野）+ come（到达）。它的力量在于：结果是“走出来”、现在能被看见的东西。

items.en: Twentieth-century medicine, education, and statistics turned outcome into a countable endpoint: patient outcome, learning outcome, primary outcome.
items.cn: 20 世纪的医学、教育与统计学把 outcome 变成可计数的终点：patient outcome、learning outcome、primary outcome。

note.en: The first group separates other out- compounds; the second ranks the main synonyms by where they place the result.
note.cn: 第一组把其他 out- 复合词分开；第二组按“结果被放在哪里”来区分主要近义词。

entries.definition: the amount produced by a machine, worker, or system. It is what is put out, not the situation that results.
entries.definitionCN: 机器、工人或系统的产出量。它是“被放出来的量”，不是最终形成的局面。

entries.definition: the sudden start of disease, war, or violence. It names a breaking out, not a result.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病、战争或暴力的突然爆发。它指“破壳而出”，不是结果。

entries.definition: a view or forecast. It is what you look out at, or forward to, not what came out.
entries.definitionCN: 景色；前景展望。它是你向外看、向前看的东西，不是出来的结果。

entries.definition: what happens because of something else. It is the broadest term and can name anything from a sum to a consequence.
entries.definitionCN: 因另一事物而发生的事。它是最宽泛的词，可以指从计算结果到后果的任何东西。

entries.definition: a result that follows logically or causally, often with a sense of importance or responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 按逻辑或因果随之而来的结果，常含重要性或责任意味。

entries.definition: the change produced by a cause. It stresses the change itself rather than the final situation.
entries.definitionCN: 原因造成的变化。它强调变化本身，而不是最终局面。

entries.definition: the final or eventual result of a series of events. It is informal and stresses the end of a long story.
entries.definitionCN: 一系列事件最终的结局。它较口语化，强调一个长故事的最后收束。

normalIntro.en: Five spelling hooks, then three abstract pictures of a process arriving at its end.
normalIntro.cn: 先给五个拼写钩子，再用三个“过程抵达终点”的抽象画面。

normal.en: out + come: what comes out at the end.
normal.cn: out + come：最后“走出来”的那个东西。

normal.en: outcome ends in -come just as become: something becomes visible at the end.
normal.cn: outcome 和 become 一样以 -come 结尾：某物在最后变得可见。

normal.en: An election outcome is the scoreboard after the last vote is counted.
normal.cn: 选举的 outcome 就是最后一张票计完后那块记分牌。

normal.en: Learning outcomes are written before the course, like a destination on a ticket.
normal.cn: learning outcomes 写在课程之前，像车票上的目的地。

normal.en: Primary outcome is the one number a trial promises to report.
normal.cn: primary outcome 是一项试验承诺要报告的那个数字。

abstract.en: An outcome is the shape a process leaves behind after it stops moving.
abstract.cn: 结果是过程停止运动后留下的那个形状。

abstract.en: You can design an outcome without being able to control it: the end is a target, not a guarantee.
abstract.cn: 你可以设计一个结果，却无法控制它：终点是目标，不是保证。

abstract.en: Every decision sends something out into the world, and that something comes back as the room you live in.
abstract.cn: 每个决定都往世界里送出某样东西，而那样东西会作为你居住的房间返回。

examples.en: No one could predict the outcome of the talks.
examples.cn: 没有人能预测会谈的结果。

examples.en: The study measured three outcomes: pain, mobility, and sleep quality.
examples.cn: 这项研究测量了三个结局指标：疼痛、活动能力与睡眠质量。

examples.en: A good process does not always produce a good outcome.
examples.cn: 好的过程并不总能产生好的结果。

dict_mnemonic.note: 记成“从过程里走出来（out）并到达（come）的东西”。
dict_mnemonic.text: out（向外）+ come（来）→ 出来的结果 → 结果、结局

root: 英语本族复合词：out（向外、进入视野）+ come（来）；1788 年见于苏格兰英语，无拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: The senses go from any result, to consequences and contest results, then to measured endpoints in medicine, education, law, and statistics.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从任何“结果”出发，走到后果与比赛结果，再到医学、教育、法律与统计中可测量的终点。

core.en: A path reaching its end, where a mark is left behind
core.cn: 一条路走到尽头，在那里留下一个印记

branches.en: General result: what an event or process finally produced.
branches.cn: 一般结果：一个事件或过程最终产生的东西。

branches.en: Formal endings: the result of a contest, or of a legal case.
branches.cn: 正式终点：比赛的结果，或案件的结果。

branches.en: Measured endings: a patient's health result, or a study's primary endpoint.
branches.cn: 可测量的终点：患者的健康结果，或研究的主要终点。

branches.en: Ends declared in advance: a hoped-for result, or a learning outcome.
branches.cn: 事先声明的终点：期望的结果，或学习成果。

branches.en: Consequence: the word looks back at what a decision cost.
branches.cn: 后果：这个词回看一个决定付出了什么代价。

intro.en: Outcome belongs to the huge out- family and the even larger come family. Both halves are native English, so there is no Latin root here.

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies: out is Old English ut, from Proto-Germanic *ut-, and come is Old English cuman, from Proto-Germanic *kwem-.

definition_zh: 嘴唇；边缘；口沿；不逊的话；（兰花的）唇瓣
definition_en: either of the two soft edges of the mouth, the rim of an opening, rude talk, or the lower petal of an orchid
core_image: 两片柔软的唇轻轻合拢，嘴角压成一条浅浅的缝
scene: 冬天的风把孩子的嘴唇吹得发红，他忍不住舔了舔。 The cold wind left her lips dry and cracked.
sceneCN: 这里 lip 是「嘴唇」（第 1 个义项：嘴的两片软边）；句意为冷风把她的嘴唇吹得又干又裂。图中可辨识物件：冻红的脸、干裂的嘴角、竖起的衣领。

pos.zh: 嘴唇；边缘；口沿；不逊的话；（兰花的）唇瓣

derivatives.zh: 由 lip 加 -y 构成，义为「爱顶嘴的；无礼的」，多用于英式口语
由 lip 与 stick 复合，义为「口红」
由 lip 与 read 复合，义为「看口型读懂话」
由 lip 与 sync 复合，义为「对口型假唱」

senses.title: Either of the two soft edges of the mouth
senses.definition: either of the two soft, movable edges that close the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 闭合嘴部的两片柔软、可活动的边缘
senses.example: He pressed his lips together and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 他抿紧嘴唇，什么也没说。
senses.why: Old English lippa named the fleshy edge of the mouth, and that body part is still the word's centre; every later sense is cut to its outline.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lippa 指的就是嘴边的肉，这个身体部位至今仍是词的核心；后来每个义项都是照着它的轮廓剪出来的。

senses.title: The rim of a container or opening
senses.definition: the edge or rim of a container, hole or opening, especially one that curves outward
senses.definitionCN: 容器、洞口或开口的边缘，尤指略微向外翻的口沿
senses.example: She wiped the lip of the cup before pouring.
senses.exampleCN: 倒水之前她擦了擦杯口。
senses.why: A mouth is a soft edge around an opening, and a cup or a crater has the same outline; English borrows the body word for any raised rim.
senses.whyCN: 嘴是围在开口周围的一圈软边，杯子和火山口也有同样的轮廓；英语便借这个身体词来指任何凸起的边沿。

senses.title: Rude or disrespectful talk
senses.definition: rude or disrespectful remarks, especially when a younger person answers back
senses.definitionCN: 无礼、不敬的话，尤指晚辈对长辈顶嘴
senses.example: Don't give me any lip about the chores.
senses.exampleCN: 别为了家务跟我顶嘴。
senses.why: Speech comes out of the mouth, and the lip is the visible gate of the mouth; insolent words are pictured as something pushed through that gate.
senses.whyCN: 话从嘴里出来，嘴唇就是嘴看得见的门；无礼的话被想成硬从这扇门里推出来的东西。

senses.title: The lower petal of an orchid
senses.definition: the lower petal of an orchid, which is usually larger and differently shaped
senses.definitionCN: 兰花下方那片通常更大、形状也不同的花瓣
senses.example: The orchid's lip is marked with dark purple spots.
senses.exampleCN: 这朵兰花下方的唇瓣上带着深紫色的斑点。
senses.why: Botanists needed a name for the petal that hangs out like a lower lip, and the everyday body word was ready at hand.
senses.whyCN: 植物学家需要给那片像下唇一样探出来的花瓣起名，手边现成的身体词正好可用。

intro.en: Lip is an Old English word for the edge of the mouth; its Germanic relatives are close, but the path further back is uncertain.
intro.cn: lip 是古英语中表示「嘴的边缘」的词；它在日耳曼语族中的亲属很近，但再往前追溯则来源不确定。

items.en: Old English records lippa for the edge of the mouth, a weak noun that already meant the body part.
items.cn: 古英语用 lippa 指嘴的边缘，这是个弱变化名词，当时已经专指这个身体部位。

items.en: The word belongs to a Germanic family with Dutch lip and German Lippe; the reconstructed ancestor is usually written with a doubled consonant, though its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词属于一个日耳曼语族，与荷兰语 lip、德语 Lippe 同族；重构的祖形通常写作带双辅音的形式，但确切形态不确定。

items.en: Beyond Germanic the origin is uncertain; a link with Latin labium has been suggested but is not reliably established.
items.cn: 再往上追溯来源不确定；有人提出它与拉丁语 labium 有关，但并未可靠证实。

items.en: Middle English lippe continues the bodily sense and settles the modern spelling without adding new meanings.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lippe 延续了身体部位的义项，并稳定了现代拼写，没有增加新的意思。

items.en: Modern English extends lip to the rim of vessels, to insolent speech, and to the lip-shaped petal of an orchid.
items.cn: 现代英语把 lip 扩展到器皿的口沿、无礼的言语，以及兰花的唇状花瓣。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and derivatives built on lip plus one Latin word for a lip; the near-meaning group collects words for mouths and edges.
note.cn: 形近组收由 lip 构成的复合词、派生词，以及一个意为「唇」的拉丁词；近义组收表示嘴与边缘的词。

entries.definition: Coloured cosmetic for the lips.
entries.definitionCN: 口红；由 lip 与 stick 复合而成。

entries.definition: Inclined to answer back rudely.
entries.definitionCN: 爱顶嘴的；由 lip 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: To understand speech by watching the speaker's lips.
entries.definitionCN: 看口型读懂话；由 lip 与 read 复合。

entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示「唇」的词，解剖学也用来指唇状褶；它与 lip 只是意义相近，拼写与词源都不同。

entries.definition: The whole opening in the face used for eating and speaking.
entries.definitionCN: 嘴；脸上用来进食和说话的整个开口，lip 只是它的一部分。

entries.definition: The outer edge of a round or curved object.
entries.definitionCN: 圆形或弧形物体的外缘。

entries.definition: The outside limit of an object or area.
The top edge of a cup or the projecting edge of a hat.

normalIntro.en: The word is a short Germanic noun for the edge of the mouth, and its family keeps returning to soft rims and openings.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个简短的日耳曼语名词，指嘴的边缘；它的同族词反复回到柔软的边沿与开口。

normal.en: Old English lippa already meant the edge of the mouth, so the body part is the oldest sense and the others borrow its outline.
normal.cn: 古英语 lippa 已经指嘴的边缘，所以身体部位是最早的义项，其他义项都借用了它的轮廓。

normal.en: Dutch lip and German Lippe are close cousins, and the short word has stayed almost unchanged around the North Sea.
normal.cn: 荷兰语 lip 和德语 Lippe 是近亲，这个短词在北海两岸几乎原样保留了下来。

normal.en: Lipstick puts lip in front of stick, and the compound never loses the mouth at its centre.
normal.cn: lipstick 把 lip 放在 stick 前面，这个复合词始终没有丢掉中心那个「嘴」。

normal.en: A cup has a lip because a cup and a mouth are both soft edges around an opening.
normal.cn: 杯子有 lip，是因为杯子和嘴都是围在开口周围的一圈软边。

normal.en: To give someone lip is to push rude words through the same gate that lets food in.
normal.cn: 对某人 give lip，就是把无礼的话从同一扇也放食物进来的门里推出去。

abstract.en: A lip is a border that can open, which makes it a fitting image for the edge of anything that must let something through.
abstract.cn: 嘴唇是一道能开的边界，很适合用来比喻任何必须放东西通过的边缘。

abstract.en: The same word covers a mouth, a cup and a crater because all three are openings with a raised rim.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖嘴、杯子和火山口，因为这三者都是带凸起边沿的开口。

abstract.en: Silence is often described as pressed lips, a reminder that the mouth's edge can shut as well as speak.
abstract.cn: 沉默常被写成抿紧的双唇，这提醒人：嘴的边缘既能说话，也能关上。

examples.en: He pressed his lips together and said nothing.
examples.cn: 他抿紧嘴唇，什么也没说。

examples.en: She wiped the lip of the cup before pouring.
examples.cn: 倒水之前她擦了擦杯口。

examples.en: The orchid's lip is marked with dark purple spots.
examples.cn: 这朵兰花下方的唇瓣上带着深紫色的斑点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里普」——他顶着嘴说个不停，靠的就是这张嘴；lip 是嘴唇，也是杯口那道边。

root: 古英语 lippa（嘴唇）；与荷兰语 lip、德语 Lippe 同属一个日耳曼语族。更早的来源不确定，与拉丁语 labium（唇）的关系未获可靠证实。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the soft edge of the mouth; from it come the rim of any opening, the insolent words pushed through that gate, and the orchid petal shaped like a lip.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是嘴边的软边；由此分出任何开口的边沿、从这扇门推出去的无礼话，以及形状像唇的兰花花瓣。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two soft lips pressed together, closing an opening at its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：两片柔软的嘴唇合在一起，在开口的边缘把它关上。

branches.en: two lips meeting in a quiet line
branches.cn: 两片嘴唇轻轻合拢成一条线

branches.en: a child answering back with a pout
branches.cn: 孩子嘟着嘴顶了一句

branches.en: a jug tipped at its rim
branches.cn: 壶口倾斜，水从边沿流出

branches.en: a flower whose lowest petal hangs like a lip
branches.cn: 一朵花最低的花瓣垂下来像一片唇

branches.en: words pushing out through the mouth
branches.cn: 话从嘴里推了出来

intro.en: The word is a short Germanic noun for the mouth's edge, and English builds compounds and a suffix on that base without adding a prefix.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个简短的日耳曼语名词，指嘴的边缘；英语在这个词基上造复合词、加后缀，却没有加前缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; Latin labium means lip, but the resemblance has not been shown to rest on a shared root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；拉丁语 labium 意为「唇」，但相似之处尚未被证明来自共同词根。

definition_zh: 避难所；庇护；躲避；保护

sceneCN: 这里 shelter 是「躲避」（第 3 个义项）；句意：他们在一棵大树下避雨。

senses.title: Place of protection
senses.definition: a place that protects people from weather or danger
senses.definitionCN: 保护人们免受天气或危险的地方
senses.example: The bus stop was a poor shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 公交站是个简陋的避雨处。
senses.why: This is the basic noun sense.

senses.title: To protect
senses.definition: to protect someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 保护某人或某物
senses.example: The wall shelters the garden from wind.
senses.exampleCN: 这堵墙为花园挡风。
senses.why: The noun became a verb of protecting.

senses.title: To find cover

senses.definitionCN: 到能提供保护的地方去

normal.en: We took shelter from the rain.

normal.en: They built a shelter for the night.
normal.cn: 他们搭了个过夜的棚子。

normal.en: The animal shelter needs volunteers.

normal.en: The old shed sheltered the tools.
normal.cn: 旧棚屋保护着工具。

abstract.cn: 避难所改变天气的影响，却不阻止天气。

abstract.en: To shelter another is to lend them your walls.

core.en: A shield between a person and harm.

branches.en: A place that blocks weather.

branches.en: To stand between harm and another.

The shelterer took in the family.
