trees left to protect new growth

definition_zh: 普通的；平常的；平凡的；例行的
definition_en: normal and not special or unusual; plain and not impressive; and also fixed by rule or custom as the standard course
core_image: 一条街上并排的店门，招牌颜色都差不多，没人多看一眼
scene: 下班时分的街上，人流照常往车站走，谁也没注意招牌换了新灯。 It was an ordinary evening until the rain began.
sceneCN: 这里是「普通的、平常的」（第 1 个义项：没有特别之处）；句意为直到下雨之前，那都是个平常的傍晚。图中可辨识物件：并排的店门、招牌、往车站去的人流。

pos.zh: 普通的；平常的；平凡的；例行的

derivatives.zh: 由 ordinary 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「通常地；一般地」
由 ordinary 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「平凡；普通」
由前缀 extra-（在……之外）加 ordinary 构成，义为「非凡的；异常的」

senses.title: Not special or unusual
senses.definition: normal and not special, unusual or different from other things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 正常的，与同类事物相比没有特别、奇特或不同之处
senses.example: He ordered an ordinary coffee and sat by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一杯普通咖啡，坐在窗边。
senses.why: The Latin adjective ordinarius described what follows the regular order of things, so the ordinary is whatever fits the usual pattern.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁形容词 ordinarius 形容「按事物常规次序来的东西」，所以 ordinary 就是老老实实符合平常样子的那一个。

senses.title: Not impressive or remarkable
senses.definition: plain and not especially good, talented or interesting
senses.definitionCN: 平实无奇，谈不上出色、有才或有意思
senses.example: It was a perfectly ordinary performance, neither bad nor memorable.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一场再平凡不过的演出，不算差，也不值得记住。
senses.why: If something merely follows the usual order, it has nothing that lifts it above the line, and that absence becomes the sense of being unremarkable.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西只是照着常规次序排进去，就没有任何地方把它抬出那条线；这种「没有高出来」的缺位，就成了「不出众」的意思。

senses.title: Established and routine
senses.definition: fixed by rule or custom and regularly followed, as in ordinary business or an ordinary session
senses.definitionCN: 按规章或惯例定下来、定期照办的，如常规业务或例会
senses.example: The committee meets on ordinary business twice a month.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会每月就常规事务开两次会。
senses.why: In law and administration an ordinary procedure is the one laid down as the standard course, so the word also names what is done by rule rather than by exception.
senses.whyCN: 在法律与行政里，ordinary 程序指被规定为标准做法的那一套，所以这个词也用来指照规章办、而非特例的事情。

intro.en: Ordinary comes from the Latin adjective for what follows the usual order, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: ordinary 来自拉丁语中表示「按常规次序」的形容词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Ordo meant a row or a fixed arrangement, and it is the root of the whole family, including order and ordinary.
items.cn: ordo 指一排或固定的次序，是整个词族的根，包括 order 与 ordinary。

items.en: Ordinarius meant according to the usual order, regular or standard, as opposed to what is exceptional.
items.cn: ordinarius 意为「按通常次序的、正规的、标准的」，与例外相对。

items.en: Old French ordinaire kept the sense of usual and customary, and it supplied the form English borrowed.
items.cn: 古法语的 ordinaire 保留「通常、惯常」的意思，英语借用的正是这个形式。

items.en: Early English ordinary meant customary or usual, and the word was also a noun for an official with regular jurisdiction.
items.cn: 早期英语的 ordinary 意为「惯常的、通常的」，同时也可作名词，指拥有常规管辖权的官员。

items.en: Modern English widened it to everyday things and people, adding the weaker sense of being plain or unremarkable.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到日常事物与普通人，并添上「平实、不出众」这层较弱的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the ordinary family and its negated relative; the near-meaning group holds adjectives for what is common and unremarkable.
note.cn: 形近组是 ordinary 词族及其否定形式；近义组是表示「常见、不出奇」的形容词。

entries.definition: Usually, in most cases.
The quality of being plain or usual.
Very unusual, remarkable or far beyond the normal.
entries.definitionCN: 极不寻常的、非凡的，远超常规的。

entries.definition: Happening often or found in many places.
entries.definitionCN: 经常发生或到处可见的。

entries.definition: Happening or done most of the time.
entries.definitionCN: 多数时候会发生或去做的。

entries.definition: Simple, without decoration or special features.
entries.definitionCN: 简单、没有装饰或特别之处的。

normalIntro.en: The word carries the Latin idea of a regular row, so the mnemonics keep the picture of something placed neatly in the usual line.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「排成一行」的观念，所以联想都围绕「按平常那一行排好」的画面。

normal.en: Ordinary and order share the Latin stem ordo, a row: ordinary means staying in the usual row.
normal.cn: ordinary 与 order 共享拉丁词干 ordo（一排）：ordinary 就是留在平常那一行里。

normal.en: Ordinarily adds -ly and turns the adjective into the adverb for usually.
normal.cn: ordinarily 加 -ly，把形容词变成表示「通常」的副词。

normal.en: Ordinariness adds -ness and names the plain quality itself.
normal.cn: ordinariness 加 -ness，直接指「普通」这种性质。

normal.en: Extraordinary adds extra-, meaning outside, so it means outside the ordinary row.
normal.cn: extraordinary 加 extra-（在……之外），所以意思是「在平常那一行之外」。

normal.en: Out of the ordinary is the fixed phrase for anything unusual.
normal.cn: out of the ordinary 是表示「不寻常」的固定说法。

abstract.en: A street of shop fronts with almost the same colour: nothing asks to be looked at.
abstract.cn: 一条街的店门颜色几乎一样：没有任何一处要求你多看它一眼。

abstract.en: The word for being in the usual row is also the word for being unremarkable.
abstract.cn: 「待在平常那一行」这个词，同时就是「不出众」这个词。

abstract.en: What is ordinary today can become invisible, which is why it takes rain to make an evening noticed.
abstract.cn: 今天平常的东西会变得看不见，所以要下一场雨，一个傍晚才被注意到。

examples.en: He ordered an ordinary coffee and sat by the window.
examples.cn: 他点了一杯普通咖啡，坐在窗边。

examples.en: It was a perfectly ordinary performance, neither bad nor memorable.
examples.cn: 那是一场再平凡不过的演出，不算差，也不值得记住。

examples.en: The committee meets on ordinary business twice a month.
examples.cn: 委员会每月就常规事务开两次会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥丁纳瑞」——按着老规矩排好的那一格，谁也不会多看一眼；记住 ordinary 是普通的。

root: 拉丁语 ordo（一排、次序，属格 ordinis）派生的形容词 ordinarius（按常规次序的），经古法语 ordinaire 进入英语；ordinary 本义「照常规的」，后引申为「普通的、平凡的」。同族词有 ordinarily、extraordinary。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the usual row of things; the senses divide into what is not special, what is not impressive, and what is fixed as the standard routine.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「事物平常排成的那一行」；义项分成没有特别之处、不出众，以及被规定为标准做法三层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a street of shop fronts in nearly the same colour, with no sign trying to stand out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条街上颜色几乎相同的店门，没有一块招牌特意跳出来。

branches.en: identical shop fronts along a street
branches.cn: 一条街上彼此相似的店门

branches.en: a man ordering the same coffee as every morning
branches.cn: 一个人点着和每个早晨一样的咖啡

branches.en: a performance that leaves no line in memory
branches.cn: 一场没在记忆里留下痕迹的演出

branches.en: a committee following its printed agenda
branches.cn: 委员会照着印好的议程开会

branches.en: a form filled in the standard way
branches.cn: 一张按标准方式填写的表格

intro.en: The word joins a Latin adjective of regular order to English suffixes, and its family adds the adverb, the noun and the negated form.
intro.cn: 这个词把表示「常规次序」的拉丁形容词接到英语后缀上，词族里再加出副词、名词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family behind ordinary is the ordo family: the noun for a row, its genitive, and the adjective ordinarius.
latinIntro.cn: ordinary 背后的拉丁词族是 ordo 一族：表示一排的名词、它的属格，以及形容词 ordinarius。

definition_zh: 粗糙的；粗略的；粗暴的；艰难的
definition_en: not smooth, not exact, or harsh and difficult
core_image: 一块未经打磨的石头
scene: 她的手抚过粗糙的石墙。 Her hand moved over the rough stone wall.
sceneCN: 这里 rough 是「粗糙的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她的手抚过粗糙的石墙。

senses.title: Not smooth
senses.definition: having an uneven surface that is not smooth to touch
senses.definitionCN: 表面不平整、摸起来不光滑
senses.example: The path is rough and full of stones.
senses.exampleCN: 这条小路崎岖多石。
senses.why: The surface rises and falls under the hand.
senses.whyCN: 表面在手下高低起伏。

senses.title: Not exact
senses.definition: not exact or detailed, but close enough
senses.definitionCN: 并不精确或详细，但大体接近
senses.example: I can give you a rough estimate.
senses.exampleCN: 我可以给你一个粗略的估计。
senses.why: The outline is left unpolished, like a rough stone.
senses.whyCN: 轮廓像未打磨的石头一样留着毛边。

senses.title: Harsh
senses.definition: violent, unpleasant, or difficult to deal with
senses.definitionCN: 粗暴的、令人不快的或难以应付的
senses.example: The team had a rough season.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍经历了一个艰难的赛季。
senses.why: A rough surface becomes a rough experience.
senses.whyCN: 粗糙的表面变成艰难的体验。

intro.en: Rough comes from Old English ruh, hairy or uneven.
intro.cn: rough 源自古代英语 ruh，意为多毛的、不平的。

items.en: Ruh means hairy, shaggy, or uneven.
items.cn: ruh 意为多毛的、蓬乱的或不平的。

items.en: Related forms describe coarse surfaces.
items.cn: 相关形式形容粗糙的表面。

items.en: Rough keeps the uneven sense.
items.cn: rough 保留不平整的含义。

items.en: Rough extends to weather and behavior.
items.cn: rough 扩展到天气与行为。

items.en: Rough idea means an approximate plan.
items.cn: rough idea 意为大致的设想。

note.en: Rough is uneven; tough is strong and hard to break.
note.cn: rough 强调不平滑，tough 强调坚韧难破。

entries.definition: strong and difficult to break
a long narrow container
about or approximately
not level or smooth
close but not exact
unkind or severe

normalIntro.en: Rough starts with a surface and spreads to plans and times.
normalIntro.cn: rough 从表面开始，扩展到计划和时光。

normal.en: The rough track hurt our feet.
normal.cn: 崎岖的小路硌得我们脚疼。

normal.en: She gave a rough sketch of the room.
normal.cn: 她画了一张房间的草图。

normal.en: The ship met rough weather at sea.
normal.cn: 船在海上遭遇恶劣天气。

normal.en: Write a rough draft before the final one.
normal.cn: 定稿前先写一份草稿。

normal.en: He had a rough time after the move.
normal.cn: 搬家后他过了一段艰难日子。

abstract.en: Picture an unpolished stone under the hand.
abstract.cn: 想象手下那块未打磨的石头。

abstract.en: Imagine a pencil outline without fine details.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅没有细部的铅笔轮廓。

abstract.en: Think of a boat rocking in hard wind.
abstract.cn: 想象船在狂风中摇晃。

examples.en: The wall felt rough under my fingers.
examples.cn: 墙壁在我指下摸起来很粗糙。

examples.en: We only have a rough plan so far.
examples.cn: 目前我们只有一个粗略的计划。

examples.en: The crew faced a rough crossing.
examples.cn: 船员们经历了艰难的渡海。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rough」读起来粗粗的——摸起来不光滑是粗糙；画得不出细是粗略；日子不好过是艰难。

root: 古代英语 ruh（多毛的、不平的）→ rough，核心义「表面不平整」。

sensesIntro.en: Rough means not smooth, not exact, or harsh and difficult.
sensesIntro.cn: rough 意为不平滑、不精确，或粗暴艰难的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unpolished stone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块未经打磨的石头。

branches.en: The uneven surface is the first sense.
branches.cn: 不平整表面是第一个义项。

branches.en: An outline can be rough too.
branches.cn: 轮廓也可以是粗略的。

branches.en: Conditions and people can be harsh.
branches.cn: 环境与人也可能是粗暴艰难的。

branches.en: Both lack polish and finish.
branches.cn: 两者都缺少打磨与完善。

branches.en: A hard surface becomes a hard experience.
branches.cn: 坚硬的表面变成艰难的经历。

intro.en: Rough is a Germanic word with English adverbs and verbs.
intro.cn: rough 是日耳曼词，并在英语中派生副词与动词。

latinIntro.en: Rough has no Latin root; its family is English.
latinIntro.cn: rough 没有拉丁词根，其词族属于英语。

items.exampleCN: rough 保留不平整的意象。

definition_zh: 圆盘；磁盘
definition_en: a flat round object, or a device that stores computer data
core_image: 一张银亮的圆片在光下转出一圈亮边
scene: 那台旧机器里，一张银亮的圆片还在慢慢转。 The files were saved on a hard disk.
sceneCN: 这里 disk 指「磁盘」（第 2 个义项：计算机的存储盘）；句意是文件存在硬盘上。

senses.title: A flat round object
senses.definition: a flat round shape or object
senses.definitionCN: 扁平圆形的形状或物件
senses.example: A disk of metal lay on the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 工作台上有一个金属圆盘。
senses.why: A coin is a disc that learned to hold value.
senses.whyCN: 硬币就是学会了承载价值的圆片。

senses.title: A store for computer data
senses.definition: a device that keeps computer data on a round magnetic or optical surface
senses.definitionCN: 以圆形磁面或光面保存计算机数据的装置
senses.example: The files are on the hard disk.
senses.exampleCN: 文件在硬盘上。
senses.why: A round plate became a quiet room for memory.
senses.whyCN: 圆盘变成了一间安静的仓库，装着记忆。

intro.en: Disk and disc both come from Latin discus, a flat round object thrown in games and set on tables.
intro.cn: disk 与 disc 同出拉丁语 discus，既指游戏中投掷的扁圆物，也指桌上的平盘。

items.en: Diskos meant a quoit thrown in competition.
items.cn: diskos 指比赛中投掷的铁饼。

items.en: Discus kept both the game piece and the table plate.
items.cn: discus 同时保留游戏器具与餐桌平盘两义。

items.en: English used disc for a round flat thing.
items.cn: 英语用 disc 指圆而扁的东西。

items.en: American spelling disk named the computer medium.
items.cn: 美式拼写 disk 用来指计算机存储介质。

items.en: Disc stays for sound and light, disk for data.
items.cn: 如今 disc 多用于声音与光盘，disk 多用于数据。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the flat round shape, and the meaning group names other round holders.
note.cn: 形近组共享扁圆的形状，近义组列出别的圆形承载物。

entries.definition: a round flat object or record
a shallow plate for food
a small flexible magnetic disk
a flat round dish
a large flat serving plate
a unit that reads and writes data

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a bright circle and end with a room full of memory.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一个亮圆片开始，落到一间装满记忆的屋子。

normal.en: Disk is a flat round thing, like a coin with no face.
normal.cn: disk 是扁圆之物，像一枚没有图案的硬币。

normal.en: A hard disk hides behind a metal box.
normal.cn: 硬盘藏在一只金属盒子后面。

normal.en: A floppy disk bends, and that was its charm.
normal.cn: 软盘能弯，这正是它的可爱处。

normal.en: Disk space runs out exactly when you need it.
normal.cn: 磁盘空间总是在你最需要时用完。

normal.en: The same shape holds music, film and files.
normal.cn: 同一种形状，装着音乐、电影与文件。

abstract.en: Picture a silver circle spinning under a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一个银圆片在灯下旋转。

abstract.en: Picture a slot swallowing the disk whole.
abstract.cn: 想象一道插槽把磁盘整个吞下。

abstract.en: Picture a small light blinking while data moves.
abstract.cn: 想象数据流动时一盏小灯在闪。

examples.en: The files were saved on a hard disk.
examples.cn: 文件存在硬盘上。

examples.en: He handed me a disk with the photos.
examples.cn: 他递给我一张存着照片的磁盘。

examples.en: A disk of polished steel covered the hole.
examples.cn: 一块抛光钢圆盘盖住了那个洞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disk 记成「扁圆片」：disk 与 dish 同源，都是拉丁语 discus 那种扁圆的东西，电脑把数据也放进了这样的圆片。

root: 源自拉丁语 discus（投掷用的扁圆物），其根可追到希腊语 diskos。英语里 disc 与 disk 原本只是拼写差异，二十世纪以后逐渐分工：disc 多指唱片与光盘，disk 多指计算机的磁盘与硬盘。

sensesIntro.en: From a quoit thrown in a game to a quiet surface that keeps our files.
sensesIntro.cn: 从比赛中投出的铁饼，到安静保存文件的那个面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright metal circle turning under a lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个发亮的金属圆片在灯下转动。

chain: IT IS PUT IN A SLOT

branches.en: The first sense is simply the shape in your hand.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是手里那个形状。

branches.en: The second sense is the shape taught to remember.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是这个形状被教会了记忆。

branches.en: Both senses are flat, round and easy to stack.
branches.cn: 两个义项都扁、都圆、都好叠放。

branches.en: Both hide their contents on a surface.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把内容放在一个面上。

branches.en: Only the second sense needs a machine to speak.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项需要机器才能说话。

intro.en: Disk belongs to the discus family, where a game piece, a plate and a data store share one shape.
intro.cn: disk 属于 discus 一族，游戏器具、餐盘与数据存储共用一种形状。

latinIntro.en: Greek diskos and Latin discus give disc and disk, two spellings of one flat round idea.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 diskos 与拉丁语 discus 给出 disc 与 disk，同一个扁圆概念的两条拼写。

items.example: The disk turned without a sound.

items.meaning: a round flat object or record

items.example: A dish stood in the middle.
The old diskette held one letter.
items.exampleCN: 那张旧软盘只装了一封信。

items.example: A diskless machine booted from the network.
items.exampleCN: 一台无盘机从网络启动。

items.meaning: the heavy disc thrown in sport
music for dancing, from record discs

items.exampleCN: 一片圆盘状的云低低挂着。

definition_zh: 到达；到来；（新）到达者；新到货；到达大厅
definition_en: the act of reaching a place, the coming of an event or period, a person or thing that has just come, or the part of a building where people arrive
core_image: 列车进站，站台上的人抬起头朝出口走去
scene: 站台的显示屏刚翻到终点站，提着行李的人群朝出口涌去。 Her arrival was announced over the loudspeaker.
sceneCN: 这里 arrival 是「到达」（第 1 个义项：抵达某地的行为）；句意为「她的到达通过广播播报了」。画面中有站台、显示屏与提行李的人群。

pos.zh: 名词：到达；到来；到达者；新到货；到达大厅

derivatives.zh: arrival 的动词形式，义为「到达；抵达」
借自法语，由 arriver 加 -iste 构成，义为「暴发户；钻营上位者」

senses.title: The act of reaching a place
senses.definition: the act of reaching a place at the end of a journey
senses.definitionCN: 一段行程结束时抵达某地的行为
senses.example: Her arrival was announced over the loudspeaker.
senses.exampleCN: 她的到达通过广播播报了。
senses.why: The Latin verb first meant to reach the shore, so arrival is literally the moment a journey touches land.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词本义是「到岸」，所以 arrival 字面上就是行程触到陆地的那一刻。

senses.title: The coming of an event or period
senses.definition: the moment when an event, season, or period begins to exist or becomes present
senses.definitionCN: 某个事件、季节或时期开始出现、来临的时刻
senses.example: The arrival of spring brought blossoms to the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 春天的到来让山谷开满了花。
senses.why: Spring is imagined as a traveller: it comes, and its coming is an arrival.
senses.whyCN: 春天被想象成一个旅人：它来了，它的到来就是一次 arrival。

senses.title: A person or thing that has just come
senses.definition: a person or thing that has recently come to a place, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 刚刚来到某地的人或物，常以复数形式使用
senses.example: The hotel keeps a list of new arrivals at the front desk.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店在前台保留一份新到客人的名单。
senses.why: By a shift from the act to its result, the arrival becomes the one who has arrived.
senses.whyCN: 由动作转指结果，arrival 便成了「已经到达的那个人」。

senses.title: The place where people arrive
senses.definition: the part of an airport or station where passengers come in
senses.definitionCN: 机场或车站里旅客抵达后走出的区域
senses.example: We waited in the arrival hall for the delayed flight.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在到达大厅等那班延误的航班。
senses.why: The act gives its name to the place built for it, just as other actions name their rooms.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作把自己的名字给了专为它而建的地方，正如别的动作也会给房间命名。

intro.en: Arrival is built on arrive, and both go back to a Latin image of a boat touching the shore.
intro.cn: arrival 建立在 arrive 之上，两者都可追到「船靠岸」这一拉丁意象。

items.en: Ripa meant 'shore, bank', the edge where land meets water.
items.cn: ripa 意为「岸、河岸」，是陆地与水相接的边缘。

items.en: Ad ripa 'to the shore' became the verb arrivare, 'to reach the shore, come to land'.
items.cn: ad ripa「到岸边」合成了动词 arrivare，意为「到岸、靠岸」。

items.en: Ariver kept the travel sense but lost the river: one could now arrive anywhere.
items.cn: ariver 保留了行程义，却丢掉了河流：如今人可以去到任何地方。

items.en: Arrive is recorded in English in the fourteenth century, and arrival is its noun formed with -al.
items.cn: arrive 在十四世纪见于英语，arrival 则是它加后缀 -al 构成的名词。

items.en: The noun widened from the act of reaching land to any coming, and then to those who come and the hall they come through.
items.cn: 这个名词从「靠岸」扩到一切到来，再扩到到来的人与到来的大厅。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words close to arrival in spelling or sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for coming and appearing.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或读音与 arrival 接近的词；近义组收表示「到来、出现」的词。

entries.definition: A person or group competing with another for the same goal.
To begin to exist or to come into notice.
The verb that underlies arrival, meaning to reach a place.
entries.definitionCN: arrival 的动词形式，义为「到达某地」。

entries.definition: The approach or arrival of someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 某人或某物的临近与到来。

entries.definition: The act of becoming visible or present.
The moment an aircraft or boat reaches the ground or shore.
entries.definitionCN: 飞机或船只触地、靠岸的那一刻。

entries.definition: The act of coming in, or the place through which one comes in.
entries.definitionCN: 进入的行为，或进入时所经过的地方。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow arrival from a train platform to spring, new guests and the arrivals hall.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子让 arrival 从站台走到春天、新到的客人，以及到达大厅。

normal.en: Arrival is the end of a journey touching the platform.
normal.cn: arrival 是一段行程触到站台的那一刻。

normal.en: The arrival of spring: a season walks in.
normal.cn: 春天的到来：一个季节走了进来。

normal.en: New arrivals: the ones who have just come.
normal.cn: 新到者：刚刚到来的人。

normal.en: The arrival hall is named after the act it serves.
normal.cn: 到达大厅因它所服务的那个动作而得名。

normal.en: Arrive once meant to reach the shore.
normal.cn: arrive 曾经只表示「靠岸」。

abstract.en: One noun covers the act, the result, the person and the place.
abstract.cn: 一个名词覆盖了行为、结果、人物与地点。

abstract.en: A journey's last step can name a whole season.
abstract.cn: 行程的最后一步可以为整个季节命名。

abstract.en: The shore image survives inside every arrival.
abstract.cn: 「靠岸」的形象藏在每一次 arrival 里。

examples.en: Her arrival was announced over the loudspeaker.
examples.cn: 她的到达通过广播播报了。

examples.en: The arrival of spring brought blossoms to the valley.
examples.cn: 春天的到来让山谷开满了花。

examples.en: The hotel keeps a list of new arrivals at the front desk.
examples.cn: 酒店在前台保留一份新到客人的名单。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊，来我」——远方的人说「啊，我来啦」，拖着箱子走进到达大厅：到达

root: arrive 来自拉丁语 ad ripa「到岸边」，本指船靠岸，经古法语 ariver 进入英语；arrival 是 arrive 加名词后缀 -al，字面就是「靠岸这件事」。由「靠岸」扩为一切到达，再扩为事件与季节的到来；由动作转指结果，又指到达的人与新到的货物；动作还给专门容纳它的场所命名，于是有了 arrival hall。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses grow from one journey's end: the act of reaching, the coming of an era, the person or thing that comes, and the hall built for coming.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项从一段行程的终点长出来：抵达的动作、时代的到来、到来的人与物，以及为到来而建的厅堂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a train pulling into a platform while travellers lift their heads toward the exit.
core.cn: 核心意象：列车进站，旅客们抬头朝出口走去。

branches.en: THE JOURNEY LINE: arrival is the moment a trip touches its end.
branches.cn: 行程线：arrival 是旅途触到终点的那一刻。

branches.en: THE SEASON LINE: events and periods are imagined as travellers.
branches.cn: 季节线：事件与时期被想象成旅人。

branches.en: THE GUEST LINE: the act gives its name to the one who performed it.
branches.cn: 来客线：动作把名字给了完成它的人。

branches.en: THE HALL LINE: a place is named after the act it serves.
branches.cn: 大厅线：场所因它所服务的动作而得名。

branches.en: THE WELCOME LINE: every arrival is both an event and a person to greet.
branches.cn: 迎接线：每一次到达既是一个事件，也是一个要迎接的人。

intro.en: Arrival is arrive plus the noun suffix -al, and the verb itself came through French from Latin.
intro.cn: arrival 是 arrive 加名词后缀 -al，动词本身经法语来自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin word ripa 'shore' also left riparian in English, and the same shore word stands behind river.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ripa「岸」还给英语留下了 riparian，而表示河流的 river 背后也是同一个「岸」字。

definition_zh: 攻击；抨击；（疾病）发作
definition_en: to use force against someone, to criticize strongly, or a sudden onset of illness
core_image: 一只手突然伸向对方
scene: 报纸头版猛烈批评了这项决定。 The paper attacked the decision on its front page.
sceneCN: 这里 attack 是「抨击」（第 2 个义项：用言语猛烈批评）；句意是报纸在头版抨击这项决定。

senses.title: Use force against
senses.definition: to try to hurt or defeat someone with force
senses.definitionCN: 用武力伤害或击败对方
senses.example: The soldiers attacked the bridge at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们在黎明时进攻那座桥。
senses.why: Attack comes from Italian attaccare, 'to join battle', from a word meaning to fasten, so the core picture is closing with an enemy and engaging.
senses.whyCN: attack 来自意大利语 attaccare「接上打斗」，其词根意为「接合」，所以核心画面是贴近敌人、交上手。

senses.title: Criticize strongly
senses.definition: to criticize someone or something very strongly in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在言语或文字中猛烈批评某人某事
senses.example: The paper attacked the decision on its front page.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸在头版抨击这项决定。
senses.why: A verbal assault borrows the whole martial image: words are aimed and driven at a target as if they were blows.
senses.whyCN: 言语上的攻击借用了整套交战画面：话像拳头一样被瞄准并砸向目标。

senses.title: Sudden onset of illness
senses.definition: a sudden and severe start of an illness
senses.definitionCN: 疾病突然而猛烈地开始
senses.example: He had a heart attack last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他去年冬天心脏病发作。
senses.why: Illness arrives like an enemy raid, so its sudden onset is named with the same word as a military strike.
senses.whyCN: 疾病像敌军突袭一样到来，所以它突然开始的那一刻，就用与军事打击相同的词来命名。

intro.en: Attack entered English from Italian fighting speech and spread from battle to words and illness.
intro.cn: attack 从意大利语的交战用语进入英语，又从战场扩展到言语与疾病。

items.en: attaccare meant 'to join battle'.
items.cn: attaccare 意为「接战、交上手」。

items.en: The phrase meant 'to begin a fight'.
items.cn: 这一短语意为「开始战斗」。

items.en: attaquer carried the military sense into French.
items.cn: attaquer 把军事含义带入法语。

items.en: English attack covered armed assault.
items.cn: 英语 attack 指武装攻击。

items.en: The word extended to criticism and to illness.
items.cn: 词义扩展到批评与疾病发作。

note.en: The look-alike group is the attack family; the near-meaning group gives verbs of striking and criticizing.
note.cn: 形近组是 attack 词族；近义组是表示打击与批评的动词。

normalIntro.en: Attack began as joining battle, and its force carries into words and illness.
normalIntro.cn: attack 起初是「交上手」，这股力道也带进了言语与疾病。

normal.en: It works as both verb and noun: to attack, an attack.
normal.cn: 它既是动词也是名词。

normal.en: Medical use always has an article or a modifier: a heart attack.
normal.cn: 医学用法通常带冠词或修饰语：心脏病发作。

normal.en: Under attack means being criticized or struck.
normal.cn: under attack 表示受到攻击或批评。

normal.en: The double t belongs to the stem: at-tack.
normal.cn: 双 t 属于词干。

normal.en: Attack the problem means tackle it eagerly.
normal.cn: attack the problem 指积极着手解决。

abstract.en: See a hand shooting out toward another.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手猛地伸向对方。

abstract.en: See a front page with a headline like a fist.
abstract.cn: 想象头版标题像一记拳头。

abstract.en: See a chest clutched in a crowded street.
abstract.cn: 想象拥挤街道上有人捂住胸口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 意大利语 attaccare 是「接战」：贴近对手动手是攻击；把话当拳头砸过去是抨击；疾病突然扑上来是发作。

root: 源自意大利语 attaccare「接战」，与表示「接合」的词根有关，经法语 attaquer 进入英语；由武力进攻引申为言语抨击，再引申为疾病突发。

sensesIntro.en: An enemy, a critic and an illness all arrive suddenly and with force.
sensesIntro.cn: 敌人、批评者与疾病，都是突然而猛烈地扑上来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand launched at a target.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手朝目标猛伸过去。

intro.cn: 这个词与 attach 外形相近，不过词义早已分开。

latinIntro.cn: 这个意大利语词干源自日耳曼语，而非拉丁语。

definition_zh: 影响；使感动；侵袭；感染；假装；喜好使用；（心理学）情感
definition_en: to produce a change in something, to move someone emotionally, to attack the body, to pretend to have a feeling, or, as a noun, an emotional state
core_image: 一颗石子落进静水，波纹一圈圈推到岸边
scene: 暴雪过后，果园的枝条一夜之间全黑了。 The early frost affected every tree in the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 affect 指低温对果树造成侵害（第 3 个义项：疾病、霜冻等侵袭身体或作物）；句意为早霜影响了谷地里的每一棵树。

pos.zh: 动词：影响；使感动；侵袭；感染；假装；喜好使用
名词（心理学）：情感；情感状态，重音在首音节

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 affectus 经法语进入英语，加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「喜爱；感情」
由 affection 加形容词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「深情的；表示爱意的」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「情感的；感情方面的」
由过去分词转成形容词，义为「受影响的」或「做作的」
由否定前缀 dis- 加 affected 构成，义为「不满的；不再忠心的」

senses.title: To produce a change in something
senses.definition: to make a difference to something or someone; to change a situation, a feeling or a result
senses.definitionCN: 对某事或某人产生作用，改变其状况、感受或结果
senses.example: Rising sea levels will affect coastal cities first.
senses.exampleCN: 海平面上升将首先影响沿海城市。
senses.why: Latin afficere meant to do something to a thing: ad- 'towards' plus facere 'do' gives the picture of an action reaching its object and leaving a mark.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 afficere 意为「对某物做点什么」：ad-「朝向」加 facere「做」，画面是一个动作落到对象身上并留下痕迹。

senses.title: To move someone emotionally
senses.definition: to cause a strong feeling in someone, especially sadness or sympathy
senses.definitionCN: 引起某人强烈的情感，尤指悲伤或同情
senses.example: The photographs of the flooded village affected her deeply.
senses.exampleCN: 那些被淹村庄的照片深深触动了她。
senses.why: The action reaching a person lands on the feelings rather than on circumstances, so the same verb names an emotional mark left behind.
senses.whyCN: 动作落到人身上时，落点是感情而不是处境，于是同一个动词就表示留在心里的那一道痕迹。

senses.title: To attack the body or a crop
senses.definition: of a disease, pest or harmful condition, to attack and damage a person, an animal or a crop
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病、害虫或有害状况侵袭并损害人、动物或作物
senses.example: The early frost affected every tree in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 早霜影响了谷地里的每一棵树。
senses.why: Here the action is violent and physical: something outside reaches the body and works on it, which is the oldest medical use of the Latin verb.
senses.whyCN: 这里的动作猛烈而具体：外来的东西侵到身体上并起作用，这正是这个拉丁动词最早的医学用法。

senses.title: To pretend to have a feeling or manner
senses.definition: to behave as if you have a feeling, quality or way of speaking that you do not really have
senses.definitionCN: 故意表现出并不真实具备的情感、气质或说话方式
senses.example: He affected a British accent to amuse the children.
senses.exampleCN: 他故意带上一口英国腔逗孩子们开心。
senses.why: The word turns back on the person: instead of reaching an object, the person puts on a surface and keeps it up, which is why this sense is close to feign.
senses.whyCN: 这时动作折回到人自己身上：不是作用于对象，而是给自己套上一层表面并刻意维持，所以这个义项接近「假装」。

senses.title: To use or wear something by preference
senses.definition: to choose to use, wear or adopt something regularly, often to create a certain impression
senses.definitionCN: 出于偏好而经常使用、穿戴或采用某物，常为营造某种印象
senses.example: She affects a plain black coat and never wears colour.
senses.exampleCN: 她总爱穿一件素黑外套，从不穿彩色衣服。
senses.why: Pretending settles into habit: what began as putting on a manner becomes the style a person keeps choosing.
senses.whyCN: 「装出来」久了就变成习惯：最初套上的一层姿态，后来成了这个人一再选择的风格。

senses.title: Emotion as a psychological term
senses.titleCN: 情感；情感状态（心理学名词）
senses.definition: in psychology, the observable outward feeling or emotional state, pronounced with the stress on the first syllable
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指可观察到的外显情感或情感状态，重音落在第一个音节
senses.example: The patient showed a flat affect throughout the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 整个面谈过程中，病人表现出情感平淡。
senses.why: The noun keeps the Latin affectus 'a state produced in the mind'; psychology took that old participle and made it a technical label.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了拉丁语 affectus「在心里造成的状态」；心理学把这个旧分词借来，当作专门的术语。

intro.en: Affect comes from a Latin verb built on 'to do', and the same Latin stock also produced effect with a different prefix.
intro.cn: affect 来自一个以「做」为核心构成的拉丁语动词；同一拉丁语词源加上不同前缀，又产生了 effect。

items.en: *dhe- is generally reconstructed as 'to put, to do', and Latin facere is usually traced to it; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *dhe- 意为「放置、做」，拉丁语 facere 通常被追溯到它；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The recorded verb facere 'to do, make' built a large family, among them factum 'a deed' and efficere 'to bring about'.
items.cn: 有文献记录的动词 facere「做、制造」衍生出庞大的词族，其中有 factum「行为、事迹」与 efficere「促成」。

items.en: Ad- 'towards' plus facere formed afficere, 'to do something to a person or thing, to influence or move'; its participle affectus meant 'a state produced in mind or body'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 facere 构成 afficere，意为「对人或物做点什么、施加影响」；其分词 affectus 指「在心里或身上造成的状态」。

items.en: The noun affectus and the French verb affecter carried both the 'influence' sense and the 'put on a show' sense into English.
items.cn: 名词 affectus 与法语动词 affecter 把「影响」和「做出样子」两种含义一并带进了英语。

items.en: Affect and effect both descend from facere but from different prefixes: affect from ad- 'to', effect from ex- 'out'. The psychological noun keeps the first-syllable stress.
items.cn: affect 与 effect 都出自 facere，但前缀不同：affect 来自 ad-「朝向」，effect 来自 ex-「出」。心理学的名词义保留首音节重音。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the facere family, with effect first because it is the word most often confused with affect; the near-meaning group holds verbs of changing, touching, infecting and pretending.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 facere 词族展开，effect 排在最前，因为它是最容易与 affect 混淆的词；近义组收表示改变、触动、感染与假装的动词。

entries.definition: A noun meaning a result or an influence, and a formal verb meaning to bring something about; it comes from ex- plus facere, 'to do out, bring about'.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结果、效果」，作动词时义为「实现、促成」；与 affect 同出拉丁语 facere，但 effect 来自 ex-「出」，指做出来的结果，affect 来自 ad-「向」，指作用到对象上，两者不可互换。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning influenced, or artificial and insincere in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受影响的」，或指举止「做作的、不自然的」。

entries.definition: A feeling of fondness or love, from the same Latin participle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「喜爱、感情」，由同一拉丁语分词 affectus 经法语进入英语。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to emotion or feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「情感的、感情方面的」，多用于心理学与教育语境。

entries.definition: To change how someone acts or thinks, usually gradually; broader and less physical than affect.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「影响」，多指逐渐改变他人的行为或想法，范围比 affect 宽，身体色彩更弱。

entries.definition: To have a strong effect on something; stronger and more forceful than affect.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「冲击、产生影响」，力度比 affect 强，常暗示明显的震动。

entries.definition: To cause strong feelings in someone, especially sympathy or sadness.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「打动、使感动」，与 affect 的第 2 个义项接近，但更口语、更强调情感反应。

entries.definition: To pass a disease into a body, or to make someone share a feeling; narrower than affect.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「传染、感染」，既可指疾病进入身体，也可指情绪传染，比 affect 的侵袭义更具体。

entries.definition: To pretend to have a feeling or condition; a formal near-match for the 'pretend' sense of affect.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「假装、佯装」，与 affect 的假装义接近，但语气正式，且不含「惯常穿戴」的引申。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin prefix and verb, the affect-effect pair, and the sentence frames the word takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据真实的拉丁语前缀与动词、affect 与 effect 的配对，以及这个词实际使用的句型。

normal.en: ad plus facere means to do something to: affect is the action landing on an object.
normal.cn: ad 加 facere 意为「对……做点什么」：affect 就是落到对象身上的那个动作。

normal.en: Effect begins with e for exit: it is the result that comes out; affect begins with a for an action aimed at something.
normal.cn: effect 以 e 开头，联想「出来」的结果；affect 以 a 开头，联想「作用于」某物的动作。

normal.en: If the sentence needs a noun for a result, the word is almost always effect.
normal.cn: 句子需要一个表示「结果」的名词时，几乎总是用 effect。

normal.en: The noun affect is a psychology term and carries the stress on the first syllable.
normal.cn: 作名词的 affect 是心理学术语，重音落在第一个音节。

normal.en: Doctors say a disease affects the lungs; patients feel the effects afterwards.
normal.cn: 医生说疾病 affects 肺部；病人随后感受到的是 effects。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropped into still water, rings spreading outward until they touch the bank.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子落进静水，涟漪一圈圈荡开，直到触到岸边。

abstract.en: The rings are the change; the stone is the cause, and the bank is whatever gets touched.
abstract.cn: 涟漪是变化，石子是原因，而岸边就是被触及的那一方。

abstract.en: The same word can touch a mood, a lung or a voice: the surface differs, the reaching does not.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以触及情绪、肺，或一口腔调：表面不同，伸手去够的动作却一样。

examples.en: Rising sea levels will affect coastal cities first.
examples.cn: 海平面上升将首先影响沿海城市。

examples.en: The photographs affected her more than she expected.
examples.cn: 那些照片对她的触动比她预想的更大。

examples.en: This decision affects everyone in the department.
examples.cn: 这个决定影响到部门里的每一个人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿费克特」——阿费克特伸手一推，水面荡开一圈圈波纹：影响。

root: 拉丁语 afficere「对……做点什么、作用于」，由 ad-「朝向」+ facere「做」构成；其过去分词 affectus 义为「在心里或身上造成的状态」，心理学的名词义即由此而来。同源的 effect 来自 ex- 加 facere，指「做出来的结果」。

sensesIntro.en: The six senses all start from 'doing something to': acting on a situation, on the feelings, on the body, on one's own surface, on a habit, and finally the inner state that results.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都从「对……做点什么」出发：作用于局势、作用于情绪、作用于身体、给自己套上一层表面、把表面变成习惯，最后落到由此形成的内在情感状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone dropped into still water, rings spreading until they reach the bank.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗石子落进静水，涟漪一圈圈荡到岸边。

branches.en: THE SITUATION: the action lands on circumstances and changes them.
branches.cn: 局势线：动作落到处境上，把处境改变。

branches.en: THE FEELINGS: the same action lands on a person's emotions and leaves a mark there.
branches.cn: 情感线：同一个动作落到人的情绪上，在那里留下痕迹。

branches.en: THE BODY: disease, frost or pests reach the body or the crop and damage it.
branches.cn: 身体线：疾病、霜冻或害虫侵到身体或作物上，造成损害。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: the action turns back on the speaker, first as a pose, then as a habit of dress or manner.
branches.cn: 表面线：动作折回说话人自身，先是姿态，后来变成穿戴或举止上的习惯。

branches.en: THE INNER STATE: the old participle becomes the psychological name for what is felt inside.
branches.cn: 内在线：旧分词成了心理学里指称内在感受的术语。

intro.en: Affect is a Latin verb of doing plus a prefix of direction; English suffixes then built the emotional and psychological family.
intro.cn: affect 是表示「做」的拉丁语动词加方向前缀构成的；英语后缀随后撑起了情感与心理学的一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere, afficere, affectus and efficere are all recorded, so no Latin form here is invented; only the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere、afficere、affectus 与 efficere 均有文献记录，这里没有任何拉丁形式是编造的；只有印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: It aims the action at an object.
items.exampleCN: 它把动作对准某个对象。

items.example: It is the doing verb shared with effect.
items.exampleCN: 它是与 effect 共有的「做」这个动词。

items.meaning: to do something to, to influence
items.example: It is the direct Latin source of affect.
items.exampleCN: 它是 affect 的直接拉丁语来源。

items.meaning: a state produced in mind or body
items.meaningCN: 在心里或身上造成的状态
items.example: It is the source of the psychological noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是心理学名词义的来源。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 affectus 经法语进入英语，义为「喜爱；感情」
由 affection 加形容词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「深情的」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「情感的」
由过去分词转成形容词，义为「受影响的」或「做作的」
由否定前缀 dis- 加 affected 构成，义为「不满的；不再忠心的」

definition_zh: 乡村的；农村的；田园的
definition_en: connected with the countryside rather than the city
core_image: 城市围墙之外：田垄、牛群与炊烟
scene: 公交车驶出城区，窗外是大片绿油油的田野。 They enjoyed the peaceful rural scenery on the way to the village.
sceneCN: 这里 rural 是「乡村的」（第 1 个义项：与农村而非城市相关）；句意：去村庄的路上他们欣赏着宁静的田园风光。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 后缀构成，义为「在农村；以乡村方式」
与 rural 同出拉丁语 rus（乡村），义为「乡下的；质朴的」
由 rural 加 -ize 后缀构成，义为「使具有乡村特点；使乡下化」

senses.title: Of the countryside
senses.definition: relating to the countryside or to farming areas far from cities
senses.definitionCN: 与农村或远离城市的耕作地区相关
senses.example: More than half the country's people live in rural areas.
senses.exampleCN: 该国一半以上的人口住在农村地区。
senses.why: The Latin word for open land points away from the walled city.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语的「旷野」一词直指城墙之外的天地。

senses.title: Characteristic of country life
senses.titleCN: 田园气息的；乡野风味的
senses.definition: having the qualities typical of life in the countryside, such as quiet and simplicity
senses.definitionCN: 具有乡村生活的典型气质，如宁静与质朴
senses.example: The inn keeps its rural charm with wooden beams and open fires.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小旅馆保留着木梁与炉火带来的乡村韵味。
senses.why: Whatever the countryside does well becomes an adjective for its character.
senses.whyCN: 乡村所擅长的气质，凝结成描述其风味的形容词。

senses.title: Relating to farming
senses.definition: connected with agriculture and farm work
senses.definitionCN: 与农业及农事劳动相关
senses.example: The government raised rural subsidies this year.
senses.exampleCN: 政府今年提高了农业补贴。
senses.why: Open land exists to be farmed, so rural reaches straight into agriculture.
senses.whyCN: 旷野生来就是为耕作而存在，rural 由此直通农业。

intro.en: Rural comes from Latin ruralis, from rus, the open country, as opposed to the walled town.
intro.cn: rural 来自拉丁语 ruralis，词根 rus 意为旷野乡村，与有围墙的城镇相对。

items.en: Rus means the open country, and ruralis means belonging to that open land.
items.cn: 拉丁语 rus 指旷野乡村，ruralis 意为属于这片旷野的。

items.en: The same root gives rusticus, rough and countrylike, later English rustic.
items.cn: 同一词根派生出 rusticus（乡野的、粗朴的），即英语 rustic 的来源。

items.en: Old French carried rural into the romance languages unchanged in sense.
items.cn: 古法语将 rural 原义传入罗曼语族诸语言。

items.en: Rural entered English in the fifteenth century as a learned Latin borrowing.
items.cn: 十五世纪 rural 作为学术性拉丁借词进入英语。

items.en: Rural now stands opposite urban in statistics, planning, and daily speech.
items.cn: 如今 rural 在统计、规划与日常语言中与 urban 相对成对。

note.en: Rural has look-alike words from the same Latin root and near-meaning words about the countryside.
note.cn: rural 的形近词多出自同一拉丁词根，近义词集中在乡村义场。

entries.definition: simple and typical of the countryside, sometimes rough
entries.definitionCN: 质朴的；粗犷的，与 rural 同出拉丁语 rus，更强调朴素粗朴

entries.definition: in or relating to rural places
entries.definitionCN: 在农村；以乡村方式，rural 的副词形式

entries.definition: to make a low heavy rolling sound
entries.definitionCN: 发出低沉的隆隆声，与 rural 拼写部分相同，词源无关，只是形近

entries.definition: land away from towns and cities
entries.definitionCN: 乡间；田野，名词指地本身，rural 是形容词指属性

entries.definition: relating to shepherds and idealized country life
entries.definitionCN: 田园牧歌式的；牧人的，带文学美化色彩

entries.definition: relating to land, farming, or its reform
entries.definitionCN: 土地的；农业的，多用于正式的农业政策语境

normalIntro.en: Five ways to remember rural through open land and its Latin root.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕旷野与拉丁词根的记忆路径。

normal.en: RURAL contains RUR, from Latin rus: the open country.
normal.cn: RURAL 里的 RUR 来自拉丁语 rus（旷野），词根就是乡村本身。

normal.en: RURAL is the opposite of URBAN: cows versus crowds.
normal.cn: RURAL 与 URBAN 相对：一边是牛群，一边是人潮。

normal.en: Rustic furniture and RURAL life both come from the same Latin field.
normal.cn: rustic（质朴的）与 rural 同一块拉丁语田野里长出来。

normal.en: RURAL schools are small, with one teacher for many grades.
normal.cn: 乡村学校规模小，一位老师教好几个年级。

normal.en: The RURAL bus stops at every farm gate along the lane.
normal.cn: 乡间班车在小路旁每一户农场门口都停。

abstract.en: See wheat bending in wind as far as the eye can reach.
abstract.cn: 看一望无际的麦浪在风中起伏。

abstract.en: Hear a rooster instead of traffic noise at dawn.
abstract.cn: 听清晨的鸡鸣取代了车流声。

abstract.en: Picture a fence, a field, and a farmhouse with smoke rising.
abstract.cn: 想象一道篱笆、一片田，农舍上炊烟袅袅。

examples.en: The hospital serves many small rural communities.
examples.cn: 这家医院服务着许多乡村小社区。

examples.en: Rural incomes have risen slowly in recent years.
examples.cn: 近年来农村收入增长缓慢。

examples.en: She prefers the quiet of rural France to city life.
examples.cn: 比起城市生活，她更喜欢法国乡间的宁静。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「乳肉」——乡下养牛，既出乳又出肉；rural 读音近似「乳肉」

root: 源自拉丁语 rus（旷野乡村）的形容词 ruralis，属学术性借词，十五世纪进入英语；与 rustic 同根，与 urban 相对。

sensesIntro.en: Rural moves from open land beyond the city, to the character of country life, to farming itself.
sensesIntro.cn: rural 从城市之外的旷野出发，到乡村生活的气质，再到农业本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: open farmland outside the city walls
core.cn: 核心意象：城墙之外开阔的农田

branches.en: Open land beyond the town is the base image.
branches.cn: 城郭之外的旷野是这个词的基础画面。

branches.en: The land's quietness becomes the character of life upon it.
branches.cn: 旷野的宁静沉淀为乡村生活的气质。

branches.en: Open land exists to be farmed, so rural covers agriculture.
branches.cn: 旷野为耕作而生，rural 因此覆盖农业。

branches.en: Farm work and country charm are two faces of the same field.
branches.cn: 农事劳作与田园风情是同一片田野的两副面孔。

branches.en: Urban and rural divide every map into two colors.
branches.cn: urban 与 rural 把每张地图分成两种颜色。

intro.en: Rural keeps a small learned family built on Latin rus.
intro.cn: rural 的词族小巧而学术，都建立在拉丁语 rus 之上。

latinIntro.en: Rural comes from Latin ruralis, built on rus, so it has Latin-rooted relatives.
latinIntro.cn: rural 来自拉丁语 ruralis（建立在 rus 之上），故有拉丁同根词。

items.meaning: in a rural way or place
items.example: Rurally located schools need more teachers.
items.exampleCN: 地处乡村的学校需要更多教师。

items.example: They ate at a rustic wooden table.
items.exampleCN: 他们坐在粗朴的木桌旁用餐。

items.example: The park ruralized the edge of the city.
items.exampleCN: 这座公园让城市边缘有了田园气息。
农村地区缺少高速网络。

items.meaning: the movement of people from the country to cities
items.example: The rural exodus emptied many villages.
items.exampleCN: 农村人口外流使许多村庄空心化。
画家们钟爱这片田园风光。

items.example: The clinic serves five rural communities.
items.exampleCN: 诊所服务五个乡村社区。

items.meaningCN: 乡村人口流失（青年进城）
items.example: Rural flight worries the local mayor.
items.exampleCN: 青年外流令当地镇长担忧。

items.meaningCN: 土地的；农业的（同场域近亲）
items.example: The country passed an agrarian reform law.
items.exampleCN: 该国通过了土地改革法。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 乡村的（rural 的直接来源）

definition_zh: 证书；证明书；凭证
definition_en: an official document that proves a fact, a qualification or an achievement
core_image: 一张盖了章、写满事实的纸
scene: 考试通过后，她拿到一张盖着红章的纸。 The school gave her a certificate.
sceneCN: 这里 certificate 指「证书」（第 1 个义项：证明资格或成就的正式文件）；句意是学校发给她一张证书。

senses.title: A document of qualification
senses.definition: an official paper showing that a person has completed a course or gained a skill
senses.definitionCN: 表明某人完成课程或获得技能的正式文件
senses.example: She has a teaching certificate.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一张教师资格证书。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to make certain, and a certificate is the paper that makes a fact certain to others.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「使确定」，而证书就是把某件事向他人确定下来的那张纸。

senses.title: Written proof of a fact
senses.definition: a document that records a fact such as a birth, a marriage or an ownership
senses.definitionCN: 记录出生、婚姻或所有权等事实的文件
senses.example: Bring your birth certificate to the office.
senses.exampleCN: 把出生证明带到办公室。
senses.why: Births and marriages are facts that must be proved to strangers, so the same paper that makes them certain records them.
senses.whyCN: 出生与婚姻都是必须向陌生人证明的事实，于是同一张使事实确定的纸也承担了记录功能。

intro.en: Certificate joins the Latin words for sure and to make, so it names a paper that makes a matter sure.
intro.cn: certificate 把拉丁语中「确定」与「做」两个词合在一起，指使事情确定下来的纸。

items.en: Certus meant settled, and facere meant to make or do.
items.cn: 拉丁语 certus 意为已定，facere 意为制作或做。

items.en: Certificare meant to make something certain in writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 certificare 意为以书面方式使某事确定。

items.en: Medieval French certificat named the written document itself.
items.cn: 中古法语 certificat 直接指这份书面文件。

items.en: English certificate first names an official written statement.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语 certificate 先指正式的书面陈述。

items.en: The word covers birth certificates, school certificates and certificates of origin.
items.cn: 这个词涵盖出生证明、学业证书与原产地证书。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the cert- family of official proof, while the meaning group lists other papers and awards.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示官方证明的 cert- 词族展开，近义组列出其他文件与奖项。

entries.definition: to state officially that something is true
the act of certifying
officially approved in writing
an official permission to do something
a paper given on completing a course
entries.definitionCN: 完成课程后获得的文书

entries.definition: a written or printed record

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into make plus certain and attach it to the papers people keep.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把词拆成「使」加「确定」，并把它挂到人们保存的那些纸上。

normal.en: Cert plus ficare: make certain. A certificate is a paper that makes a fact certain.
normal.cn: cert 加 ficare，意为使确定；certificate 就是让事实确定下来的纸。

normal.en: Birth certificate, marriage certificate and certificate of origin are three common papers.
normal.cn: 出生证明、结婚证书与原产地证书是三种常见文件。

normal.en: To issue a certificate is to hand over official proof.
normal.cn: issue a certificate 就是交出官方证明。

normal.en: Certify is the verb, certification the act, and certificate the paper.
normal.cn: certify 是动词，certification 是行为，certificate 是那张纸。

normal.en: A certificate course ends with a paper rather than a degree.
normal.cn: certificate course 以一张证书而非学位收尾。

abstract.en: Picture a red stamp landing on a clean sheet of paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚红章落在一张干净的白纸上。

abstract.en: Picture a frame on a wall holding one precious sheet.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一个相框里只装着一张珍贵的纸。

abstract.en: Picture a desk drawer where every important paper is kept.
abstract.cn: 想象一个抽屉，专门存放每一张重要文件。

examples.en: You need a medical certificate to join the course.
examples.cn: 参加这门课程需要一份体检证明。

examples.en: The certificate was signed by the head teacher.
examples.cn: 这张证书由校长签署。

examples.en: Keep your certificates in a safe place.
examples.cn: 把证书放在安全的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: cert 是「确定」，fic 是「做」：把确定的事做在纸上，就是证书。

root: 源自拉丁语 certificare（使确定），由 certus（已定的）与 facere（做）复合，经中古法语 certificat 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: One sense covers proof of skill, and the other covers proof of a recorded fact.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项覆盖技能证明，另一个义项覆盖被记录事实的证明。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of paper that turns a claim into an official fact.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张把说法变成官方事实的纸。

branches.en: The qualification sense proves a completed course or skill.
branches.cn: 资格义证明完成的课程或技能。

branches.en: The fact sense records birth, marriage or ownership.
branches.cn: 事实义记录出生、婚姻或所有权。

branches.en: Both make a claim certain through official writing.
branches.cn: 两者都通过官方书写使某种说法确定。

branches.en: Certificate courses build towards this first sense.
branches.cn: 证书课程朝着第一个义项积累。

branches.en: Birth and marriage certificates are the plainest examples of the second.
branches.cn: 出生与结婚证书是第二个义项最直白的例子。

intro.en: Certificate shares its stem with certify and certification, and -ficare marks the making.
intro.cn: certificate 与 certify、certification 同干，-ficare 标记「使…」的动作。

latinIntro.en: Certus, sure, and facere, to make, combine in certificare.
latinIntro.cn: certus（确定的）与 facere（做）在 certificare 中结合。

items.example: Show your certificate at the gate.
